```ts
      if (!pickerPlans && await coarseFitFor(ask, principal.ownerRef, billing, now) === "FREE_ROSTER") {
```

  (the body — `ask = Object.freeze({ ...ask, plan_tier: "free" as const }); substitutedAt = now;` — is B8's,
  unchanged, and so is B8's `plannedAsk = resolved.ask;` above it: the plan-decided ask stays beside a swapped one).

- `#submitWithRoom` (B6b's, as B8 leaves it — `#submitWithRoom(ask, plannedAsk, session, principal, ownership,
  room, substitutedAt)`, `plannedAsk` second and `substitutedAt` seventh — with S1a's pin): from `let createdRunId`
  to the end of the method it becomes (`type PlannedAskAdmission` is this module's own; B8's `type AskEvaluation` is
  `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof evaluateAskAdmission>>`, so it follows S2's widened return type on its own; the rest of
  B6b's method above it, its signature included, is unchanged). B8's START-only structure is carried over word for
  word — the plan's own admission beside the ask's (`plannedEvaluation`), the decision's opening choice (`keepsPlan`
  picks `runAsk` and the admission the run is created from, `evaluated`; a kept refusal is thrown before
  `recordQuery`), every `startRun` field read from that pair, and the swap-record block, START only — except that the
  ask's own admission is S2's `admitted` (B8's `swappedEvaluation`) and the one a START or a WAIT without a swap is
  created from is S2's `chosen`. With a VALID scorecard `substitutedAt` is always null, because the
  coarse fit no longer runs there, so `keepsPlan` is false and `chosen` is used unchanged; a roster-path run the
  coarse fit swapped still records its swap before its first job when it starts, and waits on its plan's own ask
  when it waits:

```ts
    let createdRunId: string | undefined;
    let setupStep: RunSetupStep = "ADMISSION_RELEASE";
    let outcome: RoomOutcome;
    // A20 (S1a): the assignment pinned inside the decision, read after the lease.
    // S2: it is the plan the decision actually pinned — the wake plan, or the plan for NOW.
    const pinned: { assignment?: AdmittedModelAssignment; personRoomTight?: boolean } = {};
    try {
      outcome = await withOwnerAskAdmissionLease(admissionPool, ownership, async (lease) => {
        // S2: the room's unlocked first look measured the person's windows; the
        // picker plans for the room at the instant this debate would start.
        const preview = await room.precheck(question);
        const admitted = await evaluateAskAdmission(this.settings, ask, personRoomOf(preview));
        // B8 (A5): the locked decision may still say WAIT (the site's day, the
        // line, or a person window that turned FULL after the coarse fit's
        // unlocked read), and a waiting question keeps its plan's ask. So when
        // the roster was swapped, the plan's own admission is taken here too,
        // still outside the decision's locks (the provider probe is cached
        // within probeFreshnessMs). Its refusal is kept as a value, not thrown:
        // it matters only if the decision says WAIT. Without a swap `plannedAsk`
        // is `ask`, and so is its evaluation. (S2: a swap happens only on the
        // roster path, which reads no person room.)
        let plannedEvaluation: AskEvaluation | AskRefusal = admitted;
        if (substitutedAt !== null) {
          try {
            plannedEvaluation = await evaluateAskAdmission(this.settings, plannedAsk);
          } catch (error) {
            if (!(error instanceof AskRefusal)) throw error;
            plannedEvaluation = error;
          }
        }
        const decided = await room.decide(question, async ({ admission, estimateMicros, now, tx }): Promise<RoomOutcome> => {
          // B8 (A5, spec §2.3.4): only a START runs on the swapped roster. A
          // question that WAITs is stored on its plan's roster and settings.
          // Nothing is written yet, so a refusal of the plan's own admission
          // rolls the decision back and no run exists.
          const keepsPlan = substitutedAt !== null && admission.kind === "WAIT";
          const runAsk = keepsPlan ? plannedAsk : ask;
          // S2: the preview said WAIT and the LOCKED decision starts it after all: the plan
          // made for NOW, never one sized for a window that has not reset yet.
          const chosen: PlannedAskAdmission = admission.kind === "START" && admitted.ifStartsNow !== undefined
            ? admitted.ifStartsNow
            : admitted;
          const evaluated: PlannedAskAdmission | AskRefusal = keepsPlan ? plannedEvaluation : chosen;
          if (evaluated instanceof AskRefusal) throw evaluated;
          await this.#liveness.recordQuery(ask.question_line, ownership, new Date(ask.as_of));
          const runId = await this.#runs.startRun({
            questionLine: runAsk.question_line,
            argumentLanguageTag: argumentLanguage.tag,
            argumentLanguageName: argumentLanguage.nameEn,
            principal,
            sessionId: session.session_id,
            callerScope: session.caller_scope,
            asOf: new Date(runAsk.as_of),
            askerRiskTier: runAsk.risk_tier,
            effectiveRiskTier: evaluated.risk.effectiveRiskTier,
            tierSource: evaluated.risk.tierSource,
            tierProvenanceRef: evaluated.risk.tierProvenanceRef,
            compositionBudgetTier: runAsk.composition_budget_tier,
            planTier: runAsk.plan_tier,
            depthParams: runAsk.depth_params,
            discoveredPanel: evaluated.discoveredPanel,
            strangerSampleRate: this.settings.strangerSampleRate,
            envelopeBasis: evaluated.envelopeBasis,
            registerVersion: this.settings.registerVersion,
            batteryVersion: this.settings.batteryVersion,
            askContract: {
              decision_scope: runAsk.decision_scope,
              steering_presets: runAsk.steering_presets,
              steering_annotations: runAsk.steering_annotations,
              critic_unavailable_cap: evaluated.criticUnavailableCap
            },
            batteryRows: createInitialBatteryRows({ settlementWatchHandle: this.settings.settlementWatchHandle })
          }, lease.client);
          createdRunId = runId;
          if (substitutedAt !== null && admission.kind === "START") {
            // B8 (budget spec §2.9): the interim swap's owner record, in the room
            // decision's own transaction. It commits with the run's hold (START),
            // or not at all; a failure rolls the decision back and records the
            // run FAILED (RUN_SETUP_FAILED:COST_RECORD). A WAIT swapped nothing.
            setupStep = "COST_RECORD";
            await this.#recordRosterSubstitution(runId, substitutedAt, tx);
          }
          // A20 × PR #33 (S1a): the pin is a setup step here too, for START and WAIT alike,
          // and it pins the admission the run was created from.
          if (evaluated.modelAssignment !== undefined) {
            setupStep = "MODEL_ASSIGNMENT";
            await insertRunRoleAssignment(this.pool, {
              runId,
              assignment: { ...evaluated.modelAssignment.assignment },
              strength: evaluated.modelAssignment.appliedStrength,
              steppedDown: evaluated.modelAssignment.steppedDown
            });
            pinned.assignment = evaluated.modelAssignment;
          }
          pinned.personRoomTight = admission.kind === "START" && evaluated.personRoomTight === true;
          setupStep = "MEMORY_QUESTION";
          await this.#serve.recordMemoryQuestion({
            runId,
            questionLine: ask.question_line,
            callerScope: session.caller_scope,
            askerScope: session.asker_id,
            asOf: ask.as_of,
            policyVersion: this.settings.registerVersion,
            ...(this.settings.memoryPullPolicy === undefined ? {} : { pullPolicy: this.settings.memoryPullPolicy })
          }, ownership);
          if (admission.kind === "WAIT") {
            setupStep = "WAITING_LINE";
            await room.enterWait(tx, runId, now);
            return Object.freeze({ kind: "WAIT" as const, runId, waitsUntil: admission.waitsUntil, scope: admission.worstScope });
          }
          setupStep = "ROOM_HOLD";
          // S2: the chosen plan's figure when the picker planned the run (its estimate, or
          // the run maximum when it could not make one); B6b's settings-class estimate otherwise.
          // A START never keeps the plan's ask, so `evaluated` is S2's `chosen` here.
          await room.openStart(tx, { runId, access: ownership, heldMicros: evaluated.pickedHoldMicros ?? estimateMicros, now });
          // LAST: nothing may follow the first job inside the decision (see RunSetupStep).
          setupStep = "WORK_QUEUE";
          const workItemId = await this.#work.enqueueOn(tx, { runId, ...firstRunJob(runId), nodeSet: [] });
          return Object.freeze({ kind: "START" as const, runId, workItemId });
        });
        // The decision committed: what can still fail inside the lease is its release.
        setupStep = "ADMISSION_RELEASE";
        return decided;
      });
    } catch (error) {
      if (createdRunId !== undefined) await this.#recordRunSetupFailure(createdRunId, setupStep);
      if (error instanceof AskAlreadyWaitingError) throw new AskAlreadyWaitingRefusal(error);
      if (error instanceof TypedDomainError && error.code === "OWNER_PRIVATE_HISTORY_SCAN_SATURATED") {
        throw new AskRefusal(error);
      }
      throw error;
    }
    const strengthFields = pinned.assignment === undefined ? {} : {
      model_strength_applied: pinned.assignment.appliedStrength,
      model_strength_stepped_down: pinned.assignment.steppedDown
    };
    if (outcome.kind === "WAIT") {
      console.info(JSON.stringify(Object.freeze({ event: "api.ask.waiting", runId: outcome.runId, scope: outcome.scope })));
      return Object.freeze({
        run_ref: outcome.runId,
        status: "WAITING" as const,
        waits_until: outcome.waitsUntil.toISOString(),
        waiting_scope: outcome.scope,
        ...strengthFields
      });
    }
    try {
      await this.dispatcher.dispatch({ runId: outcome.runId, workItemId: outcome.workItemId });
    } catch (error) {
      await this.#recordRunSetupFailure(outcome.runId, "DISPATCH");
      throw error;
    }
    // A5: nothing fitted the person's room even at ECONOMY, and it started (content-free: ids only).
    if (pinned.personRoomTight === true) {
      console.info(JSON.stringify(Object.freeze({ event: "api.ask.person_room_tight", runId: outcome.runId })));
    }
    return Object.freeze({ run_ref: outcome.runId, status: "QUEUED" as const, ...strengthFields });
  }
```

| `cost-envelope-policy.ts` (extend) | `costEnvelopePolicy` | `COST_ENVELOPE_POLICY` | `readCostEnvelopePolicy` | `COST_ENVELOPE_POLICY_DEPLOYMENT_REGISTER_ROW` (new version carries the members) | `CostEnvelopePolicy` gains `closeBasisPoints: number \| null`, `finishBasisPoints: number \| null`, `waitingLinePerPerson: number \| null` from optional members `admission_close_basis_points` (5000–10000), `finish_up_to_basis_points` (10000–20000), `waiting_line_per_person` (1–10), all-or-none refinement |
| `billing-plans.ts` | `billingPlans` | `BILLING_PLANS` | `readBillingPlans(pool, version): Promise<BillingPlans \| null>` (null = row absent) | `BILLING_PLANS_DEPLOYMENT_REGISTER_ROW` | see §3 |
| `billing-policy.ts` | `billingPolicy` | `BILLING_POLICY` | `readBillingPolicy(pool, version): Promise<BillingPolicy \| null>` (null = billing off) | `BILLING_POLICY_DEPLOYMENT_REGISTER_ROW` (`enabled: false`) | see §3 |
| `country-policy.ts` | `countryPolicy` | `COUNTRY_POLICY` | `readCountryPolicy(pool, version): Promise<CountryPolicy \| null>` | `COUNTRY_POLICY_DEPLOYMENT_REGISTER_ROW` | see §3 |
| `tax-authorities.ts` | `taxAuthorities` | `TAX_AUTHORITIES` | `readTaxAuthorities(pool, version): Promise<TaxAuthorities \| null>` | `TAX_AUTHORITIES_DEPLOYMENT_REGISTER_ROW` | P16 defines |

Also: admission policy's next version gains scopes `billingQuote` (owner, 10/h), `billingNotify` (IP, 120/min), `billingCancelLink` (IP, 5/h), `geoAvailability` (IP, 60/min); auth policy's next version gains step-up purpose `WITHDRAW_SUBSCRIPTION`. Each reader follows `readCostEnvelopePolicy`'s shape (`TypedDomainError` codes `<ROW>_INVALID`). Every new row is exported from `packages/register/src/index.ts`, added to the development seeder (`apps/runner/src/dev-deployment-register.ts`) and to `deploy/vps/register/hosted-register.example.json` + the hosted publish command's validation.

```ts
// packages/register/src/billing-plans.ts
export type PlanId = "FREE" | "PLUS" | "PRO" | "MAX";
export type FreeFixedGauges = Readonly<{ riskTier: "casual"; compositionBudgetTier: "low"; depth: number }>; // values copied from apps/ui/app/new/defaults.tsx at B4 time
export type BillingPlan = Readonly<{
  planId: PlanId;
  tier: "free" | "premium";               // PlanTier from packages/contract/src/plan-tiers.ts
  netPriceMicros: number;                 // USD micros, whole cents
  monthlyCreditMicros: number;
  dayBasisPoints: number | null;          // 2000 for paid, null for FREE
  weekBasisPoints: number | null;         // 5000 for paid, null for FREE
  finishBasisPoints: number;              // 11000
  fixedGauges: FreeFixedGauges | null;    // FREE only
}>;
export type BillingPlans = Readonly<{ currency: "USD"; plans: ReadonlyArray<BillingPlan>; sourceRef: string }>;
export function planById(plans: BillingPlans, id: PlanId): BillingPlan; // throws BILLING_PLAN_UNKNOWN

// packages/register/src/billing-policy.ts
export type BillingPolicy = Readonly<{
  enabled: boolean;
  xmoneyEnvironment: "stage" | "live";
  dunningRetryDays: ReadonlyArray<number>;      // [1, 3, 7]
  withdrawalDays: number;                       // 14
  renewalNoticeBusinessDays: number;            // 7
  lookAheadBusinessDays: number;                // 10
  confirmationBusinessDays: number;             // 2
  quoteTtlSeconds: number;                      // 1800
  taxCode: "saas" | "eservice";                 // "saas"
  invoiceIssuerRules: Readonly<Record<string, "QUADERNO" | "SMARTBILL">>; // {RO: "SMARTBILL", "*": "QUADERNO"}
  withdrawalCountries: ReadonlyArray<string>;   // EU27 + IS + LI + NO + GB (ISO2)
  sourceRef: string;
}>;

// packages/register/src/country-policy.ts
export type CountryReason = "OFFERED" | "NOT_OFFERED" | "TAX_NOT_READY" | "SANCTIONS" | "PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED" | "TERMS_EXCLUDED";
export type CountryRule = Readonly<{ signup: boolean; pay: boolean; reason: CountryReason; blocked: boolean }>;
export type CountryPolicy = Readonly<{
  defaultRule: CountryRule;                      // {signup:false, pay:false, reason:"NOT_OFFERED", blocked:false}
  countries: Readonly<Record<string, CountryRule>>; // ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 upper case
  unknownIp: "REFUSE";
  tor: "REFUSE";
  sourceRef: string;
}>;
export function countryRule(policy: CountryPolicy, iso2: string): CountryRule;

// packages/budget/src/person-allowance.ts
export type SpendScope = "SITE_DAY" | "PERSON_DAY" | "PERSON_WEEK" | "PERSON_MONTH";
export type PersonWindow = Readonly<{
  scope: Exclude<SpendScope, "SITE_DAY">;
  limitMicros: number; periodStart: Date; resetsAt: Date;
  finishBasisPoints: number; closeBasisPoints: number;
}>;
export interface PersonAllowanceSource { read(ownerRef: string, now: Date): Promise<ReadonlyArray<PersonWindow>>; }
export const NO_PERSON_ALLOWANCE: PersonAllowanceSource; // returns []

// packages/budget/src/room.ts  (B1)
export type Room = "FITS" | "CLOSE" | "FULL";
export function decideRoom(input: { usedMicros: number; estimateMicros: number; limitMicros: number; closeBasisPoints: number }): Room;
export type ScopeRoom = Readonly<{ scope: SpendScope; room: Room; resetsAt: Date }>;
export type Admission =
  | Readonly<{ kind: "START"; worst: Room; worstScope: SpendScope | null }>
  | Readonly<{ kind: "WAIT"; waitsUntil: Date; worstScope: SpendScope }>
  | Readonly<{ kind: "REFUSE_ALREADY_WAITING" }>;
export function decideAdmission(input: { rooms: ReadonlyArray<ScopeRoom>; siteLineBlocking: boolean; personWaitingCount: number; waitingLinePerPerson: number; nextTickAt: Date }): Admission;
export type Wall = "WITHIN" | "WOULD_CROSS";
export function decideSharedWall(input: { spentMicros: number; projectedMicros: number; limitMicros: number; finishBasisPoints: number }): Wall;

// packages/budget/src/estimate.ts  (B2)
export type RunSettingsClass = Readonly<{ planTier: "free" | "premium"; compositionBudgetTier: "low" | "medium" | "high"; makerCount: number; depth: number }>;
export interface CostEstimator { estimateMicros(settings: RunSettingsClass): Promise<number>; }
export class RecentRunsCostEstimator implements CostEstimator { /* B2 defines constructor */ }

// packages/billing-core/src/windows.ts  (B4)
export type TimeWindow = Readonly<{ start: Date; end: Date }>;
export function computeWindows(anchor: Date, now: Date): Readonly<{ month: TimeWindow; week: TimeWindow; day: TimeWindow }>;
export function personWindowsFor(plan: BillingPlan, anchor: Date, now: Date, closeBasisPoints: number): ReadonlyArray<PersonWindow>;
export function allowanceVsPlus(plans: BillingPlans, id: PlanId): string; // "0.04", "1", "4", "30"

// packages/billing-core/src/money.ts, subscription.ts, calendar.ts (P2)
export function microsToDecimal(micros: number): string;          // 24_200_000 -> "24.20"; refuses non-cent (BILLING_AMOUNT_NOT_CENTS)
export function decimalToMicros(decimal: string): number;         // "24.2" | "24.20" -> 24_200_000; refuses >2 decimals
export function upgradeProrationMicros(i: { oldNetMicros: number; newNetMicros: number; periodStart: Date; periodEnd: Date; now: Date }): number; // whole cents, floor
export function withdrawalRefundMicros(i: { paidTotalMicros: number; periodStart: Date; periodEnd: Date; now: Date; creditSpentMicros: number; monthlyCreditMicros: number }): number; // whole cents, floor, >= 0
export function addBusinessDays(from: Date, days: number): Date;   // Mon–Fri, UTC
export function businessDaysBetween(from: Date, to: Date): number;
export function invoiceIssuerFor(taxCountry: string, rules: BillingPolicy["invoiceIssuerRules"]): "QUADERNO" | "SMARTBILL";
export type SubscriptionEventKind = "CREATED" | "ACTIVATED" | "RENEWED" | "PAST_DUE" | "RECOVERED" | "UPGRADED" | "DOWNGRADE_SCHEDULED" | "DOWNGRADED" | "CANCEL_REQUESTED" | "CANCEL_REVOKED" | "ENDED" | "WITHDRAWN" | "SUSPENDED" | "RESUMED" | "CARD_CHANGED" | "ERASURE_STOPPED" | "RENEWAL_POSTPONED";
export type SubscriptionStatus = "CREATED" | "ACTIVE" | "PAST_DUE" | "SUSPENDED" | "ENDED" | "WITHDRAWN";
export type EndedCause = "CANCEL" | "DUNNING" | "ERASURE" | "ABANDONED";
export type SubscriptionEvent = Readonly<{ eventId: string; subscriptionId: string; ownerRef: string; kind: SubscriptionEventKind; at: Date; planId: PlanId; periodAnchorAt: Date | null; xmoneyOrderId: string | null; xmoneyCustomerId: string | null; cardRef: string | null; data: Readonly<Record<string, string | number | boolean | null>> }>;
export type SubscriptionState = Readonly<{
  subscriptionId: string; ownerRef: string; planId: PlanId; status: SubscriptionStatus;
  periodAnchorAt: Date | null; currentPeriodStart: Date | null; currentPeriodEnd: Date | null;
  cancelRequested: boolean; scheduledDowngradePlanId: PlanId | null;
  xmoneyOrderId: string | null; xmoneyCustomerId: string | null; cardRef: string | null;
  activatedAt: Date | null; endedCause: EndedCause | null; pastDueSince: Date | null; retryIndex: number;
  renewalPostponedUntil: Date | null;
}>;
export function foldSubscription(events: ReadonlyArray<SubscriptionEvent>): SubscriptionState; // throws BILLING_SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS_INVALID on an illegal transition
export function entitlementPlanOf(state: SubscriptionState): PlanId | "FREE"; // ACTIVE / PAST_DUE -> planId; else FREE

// packages/billing-core/src/ports.ts (P2)
export type TaxLocation = Readonly<{ country: string; region: string | null; postalCode: string | null; city: string | null; street: string | null; ip: string | null }>;
export type TaxStatus = "TAXABLE" | "NON_TAXABLE" | "NOT_REGISTERED" | "REVERSE_CHARGE";
export type TaxQuote = Readonly<{ netMicros: number; taxMicros: number; totalMicros: number; taxRateBasisPoints: number; taxName: string; taxCountry: string; taxRegion: string | null; status: TaxStatus; reference: string | null }>;
export type TaxIdCheck = Readonly<{ valid: boolean; name: string | null; checkedAt: Date; reference: string | null }>;
export type SaleRecord = Readonly<{ chargeId: string; transactionId: string; issuedOn: Date; customer: Readonly<{ name: string | null; email: string; country: string; region: string | null; postalCode: string | null; taxId: string | null; locale: string }>; lines: ReadonlyArray<Readonly<{ description: string; netMicros: number; taxRateBasisPoints: number }>>; taxCode: "saas" | "eservice"; evidence: Readonly<{ billingCountry: string; ipAddress: string | null; bankCountry: string | null }> }>;
export type RefundRecord = Readonly<{ chargeId: string; transactionId: string; issuedOn: Date; refundTotalMicros: number; original: Readonly<{ documentId: string; number: string }> }>;
export interface TaxEngine {
  quote(i: { netMicros: number; currency: "USD"; location: TaxLocation; taxId: string | null; taxCode: "saas" | "eservice"; date: Date }): Promise<TaxQuote>;
  validateTaxId(country: string, taxId: string): Promise<TaxIdCheck>;
  recordSale(i: SaleRecord): Promise<{ documentId: string; number: string; url: string | null }>;
  recordRefund(i: RefundRecord): Promise<{ documentId: string; number: string }>;
}
export interface InvoiceIssuer {
  issue(i: SaleRecord): Promise<{ series: string; number: string; externalRef: string }>;
  storno(i: RefundRecord & { series: string; number: string }): Promise<{ series: string; number: string; externalRef: string }>;
}
// errors: TAX_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, TAX_SERVICE_REFUSED, INVOICE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, INVOICE_SERVICE_REFUSED (TypedDomainError)
```

| `@debateai/tax-quaderno` | `packages/tax-quaderno` | `@debateai/billing-core` | `class QuadernoTaxEngine implements TaxEngine { constructor(o: {baseUrl: string; apiKey: string; fetch?: typeof fetch; timeoutMs?: number}) }` |
| `@debateai/invoice-smartbill` | `packages/invoice-smartbill` | `@debateai/billing-core` | `class SmartBillInvoiceIssuer implements InvoiceIssuer { constructor(o: {baseUrl: string; username: string; token: string; companyCif: string; series: string; fetch?: typeof fetch}) }` |
| `@debateai/mail-templates` | `packages/mail-templates` | — | `MailTemplateId`; `renderMail(id, locale, params): {subject: string; text: string; html: string}`; catalogues `messages/<locale>/mail.json` (35 locales) |

Each new package: `package.json` like `packages/budget/package.json` (`"exports": "./src/index.ts"`, private, `type: module`), registered by the workspace glob; the dependency added to the consumer's `package.json`; `pnpm install` updates the lockfile (7-day release-age cooldown: `mmdb-lib` must be a version older than 7 days — pin exact).

## 6. xMoney package (P3)

```ts
// packages/payments-xmoney/src/index.ts
export type XMoneyEnvironment = "stage" | "live";
export type XMoneyStatus = "start" | "in-progress" | "3d-pending" | "complete-ok" | "complete-failed" | "refund-ok" | "void-ok" | "cancel-ok" | "charge-back";
export type XMoneyTransaction = Readonly<{ transactionId: string; orderId: string; externalOrderId: string | null; customerId: string; cardId: string | null; status: XMoneyStatus; amountDecimal: string; currency: string; ip: string | null; transactionSource: string | null; transactionType: string | null; createdAt: Date | null }>;
export type XMoneyNotice = Readonly<{ transactionStatus: XMoneyStatus; orderId: string; externalOrderId: string | null; transactionId: string; customerId: string; amountDecimal: string; currency: string; cardId: string | null; timestamp: number | null }>;
export type XMoneyEmbeddedOrder = Readonly<{ publicKey: string; siteId: string; customer: { identifier: string; email: string; country: string }; order: { orderId: string; type: "managed"; amount: string; currency: "USD"; description: string }; cardTransactionMode: "authAndCapture" | "verifyCard"; saveCard: true; backUrl: string; customData?: string }>;
export function signOrderPayload(order: XMoneyEmbeddedOrder, privateKey: string): { payload: string; checksum: string };
export function aesKeyFromPrivateKey(privateKey: string): Buffer;      // exactly 32 bytes else XMONEY_KEY_LENGTH_INVALID (format confirmed by X0)
export function decryptNotice(opensslResult: string, privateKey: string): XMoneyNotice; // XMONEY_NOTICE_UNDECRYPTABLE
export class XMoneyClient {
  constructor(o: { baseUrl: string; privateKey: string; siteId: string; fetch?: typeof fetch; timeoutMs?: number });
  createCustomer(i: { identifier: string; email: string; country: string | null }): Promise<{ customerId: string }>;
  getTransaction(transactionId: string): Promise<XMoneyTransaction>;
  getCard(cardId: string, customerId: string): Promise<{ cardId: string; countryCode: string | null }>;
  rebill(i: { orderId: string; customerId: string; amountDecimal: string }): Promise<{ transactionId: string; orderId: string }>;
  cancelOrder(i: { orderId: string; reason: "customer-demand" | "fraud-confirm"; message: string }): Promise<void>;
  refund(i: { transactionId: string; amountDecimal: string | null; reason: "customer-demand" | "fraud-confirm"; message: string }): Promise<void>;
  listTransactions(i: { from: Date; to: Date; transactionType?: "chargeback" }): Promise<ReadonlyArray<XMoneyTransaction>>;
}
// errors (TypedDomainError): XMONEY_UNAVAILABLE (network/5xx/timeout), XMONEY_REFUSED (4xx, carries xMoney code only), XMONEY_PAYMENT_FAILED (402)
// fake: tests/support/fake-xmoney.ts — startFakeXMoney(): Promise<{ baseUrl; privateKey; publicKey; siteId; transactions: Map; completeOrder(i: {externalOrderId, amountDecimal, cardCountry, succeed: boolean}): Promise<XMoneyNotice & {opensslResult: string}>; setCardCountry(cardId, iso2); failNextRebill(code); stop(): Promise<void> }>
```

## 7. Environment (packages/register/src/runtime-environment.ts `apiEnvironmentShape`)

| Name | Required | Kind | Task |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RECORDS_KEY_PATH` | always (API) | 32-byte key file (`loadSecretKey`) | L1 |
| `GEOIP_COUNTRY_DB_PATH` | hosted | MMDB file path (public data, not custody) | G1 |
| `TOR_EXIT_LIST_PATH` | hosted | text file path | G1 |
| `XMONEY_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH` | hosted + billing on | custody text (`readCustodyAuthorizationHeader`) | P6 |
| `XMONEY_PUBLIC_KEY` | hosted + billing on | plain | P6 |
| `XMONEY_SITE_ID` | hosted + billing on | plain | P6 |
| `XMONEY_API_BASE_URL` | hosted + billing on | https URL | P6 |
| `QUADERNO_API_KEY_PATH` / `QUADERNO_API_BASE_URL` | hosted + billing on | custody text / URL | P6 |
| `SMARTBILL_CREDENTIALS_PATH` / `SMARTBILL_API_BASE_URL` / `SMARTBILL_COMPANY_CIF` / `SMARTBILL_SERIES` | hosted + billing on | custody text `user:token` / URL / plain / plain | P6 |
| `OWNER_REPORT_EMAIL_PATH` | hosted + billing on | custody text (one address) | P6 |
| `PUBLIC_SITE_ORIGIN` | hosted + billing on | https origin used for backUrl / cancel links | P6 |

"billing on" is only known after the register is read, so P6 validates the billing group at boot with `BILLING_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE` (names the missing variable). UI env (apps/ui may read process.env): `XMONEY_SDK_ORIGIN` (e.g. `https://secure-stage.xmoney.com`), unset = no billing CSP additions.

## Appendix C — Spec amendments A1–A26 (binding; also spec §2.15)


Each item: finding → resolution → affected tasks.

A1 (rebill matching). `PATCH /order-rebill/{id}` carries no id of ours; `Transaction.orderId` is xMoney's integer; `externalOrderId` lives on the Order (= our INITIAL charge id forever). RESOLUTION: before calling rebill, the charge row exists with `REQUESTED`; the rebill response's `data.transactionId` is written as a new charge_event kind `SUBMITTED` (xmoney_transaction_id set). VERIFY_PAYMENT matches a transaction to a charge in this order: (1) by `SUBMITTED.xmoney_transaction_id`; (2) only for INITIAL/CARD_CHECK: by the notice's `externalOrderId`, else `GET /order/{orderId}` → `externalOrderId`; (3) otherwise unknown → retried with backoff, then left to the reconciler. Affects P1 (kinds), P3 (client `getOrder(orderId): {orderId, externalOrderId}`), P9, P11, P12, P14.

A2 (no double charge on retry). order-rebill has no idempotency key. RESOLUTION: never resubmit a rebill whose outcome is unknown (timeout, network error, 5xx). Mark charge_event `SUBMIT_UNKNOWN`; the reconciler (and any later retry) first calls `GET /transaction?orderId=<xmoney order>&createdAtFrom=<charge created_at>` and adopts a transaction with the charge's amount; only when none exists 30 minutes after the unknown submit may the charge be submitted once more. Dunning retries (+1/+3/+7 days) create a NEW charge row each (kind RENEWAL, `attempt` 1..4, UNIQUE (subscription_id, kind, period_start, attempt)). Affects P1, P3 (listTransactions gains `orderId` + `dateType` + `createdAtFrom/To`), P11, P12, P14.

A3 (DB uniqueness against double checkout). RESOLUTION: (a) a quote is single-use: `billing.quote_use (quote_id PRIMARY KEY, used_at, charge_id)`; (b) checkout runs under the owner advisory lock (`hashtextextended('debateai.billing.owner:'||owner_ref,0)`); if a CREATED subscription younger than 30 min exists, the same charge is returned (payload re-signed) instead of a new one; older ones are ENDED(ABANDONED) first; (c) UNIQUE (subscription_id, kind, period_start, attempt) on `billing.charge`; (d) partial UNIQUE index on `billing.charge_event (charge_id) WHERE kind='SUCCEEDED'`; (e) partial UNIQUE index on `billing.outbox (kind, ref) WHERE done_at IS NULL AND dead_at IS NULL`, enqueue = `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; (f) VERIFY_PAYMENT writes charge_event + subscription_event + entitlement_event + enqueues in ONE transaction. Affects P1, P8, P9.

A4 (no double refund). RESOLUTION: (a) a refund first writes charge_event `REFUND_REQUESTED` (amount, target xmoney_transaction_id; UNIQUE (charge_id, xmoney_transaction_id, kind)) in its own committed transaction; the refund-sum guard counts REFUND_REQUESTED amounts, so the limit holds BEFORE money moves; (b) a refund spanning several transactions (INITIAL + UPGRADE) is split per transaction, newest first; (c) before any retry of a refund call, `GET /transaction/{id}`: status `refund-ok` (or a reduced refundable amount) → record `REFUNDED` without calling again; (d) managed orders are NEVER cancelled at xMoney (`DELETE /order` is only for orders without payments): stopping renewals is entirely ours (we simply stop calling rebill). Cancel, withdrawal, erasure, card change and BLOCKED-card refunds make no DELETE /order call. Affects P1, P3 (drop cancelOrder from use; keep the method unused? → remove it), P9, P12, P15.

A5 (Free must not wait forever). RESOLUTION: keep the budget spec's rule exactly — only `FULL` waits; `used + estimate > limit` is `CLOSE` and the debate STARTS (the runtime wall at the finish edge trims arguing, cheaper models first, answer always written). Spec §2.6 items 5 and 7 are amended: when nothing fits the person room even at ECONOMY (Part 3) or on the Free roster (interim), the debate starts at the cheapest choice as CLOSE; it WAITs only when a window is FULL. Affects B6, B8, S2.

A6 (upgrade gaming). RESOLUTION (owner asked separately; default until answered = prorate): on upgrade, the current period's MONTH credit becomes `old credit + (new credit − old credit) × remaining seconds ÷ period seconds` (floor to micros); day and week caps are the new plan's basis points applied to the NEW plan's full monthly credit but never above the prorated month credit. Stored on the entitlement event as `month_credit_override_micros` (null = plan credit). The next period uses the plan's full credit. Affects B4 (`personWindowsFor` takes an optional override), B5 (column), P12.

A7 (renewal-notice comparison). RESOLUTION: each subscription carries an **announced recurring total** — set at ACTIVATED (the checkout total), at UPGRADED (the new plan's recurring total quoted then), at DOWNGRADE_SCHEDULED (the lower plan's total quoted then), and at every M3 notice (`RENEWAL_NOTICE_SENT` event data `{announced_total_micros, sent_at}`). A renewal charges without notice iff its fresh quote total equals the announced total; otherwise M3 + postpone 7 business days (RENEWAL_POSTPONED). The look-ahead job sends M3 when the fresh quote differs from the announced total. Affects P2 (fold keeps `announcedTotalMicros`, `lastNoticeAt`), P11, P12.

A8 (time-driven transitions + fail-safe access). RESOLUTION: (a) every entitlement event carries `paid_through` (timestamptz, null for FREE): the current period end; extended by the dunning window (+8 days) while PAST_DUE and by a postponement while RENEWAL_POSTPONED; `person_windows_v` and `EntitlementRepository.current` treat a paid plan as FREE once `now > paid_through` — a stuck job can never leave paid access forever; (b) the renewal timer also runs a **period-end sweep**: cancel-requested → ENDED(CANCEL) + FREE entitlement anchored at the period end; CREATED older than 24 h → ENDED(ABANDONED); SUSPENDED at period end → ENDED(DISPUTE) (new EndedCause); (c) a late `complete-ok` for an ABANDONED subscription's INITIAL charge re-activates it if the owner has no other ACTIVE/PAST_DUE subscription, else it is refunded in full (A4 path) + M11-style email "refunded, you already had a plan". Affects B5, P1, P2, P9, P11, P14.

A9 (full status table). RESOLUTION: VERIFY_PAYMENT maps transaction status: `start|in-progress|3d-pending` → not final: re-enqueue with backoff 1m, 5m, 15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, then leave to the reconciler; `complete-ok` → SUCCEEDED; `complete-failed` → FAILED; `refund-ok` → REFUNDED (if no REFUND_REQUESTED of ours exists, it is a dashboard refund by the owner: record REFUNDED + credit note; the subscription is unchanged); `void-ok|cancel-ok` on a charge not yet SUCCEEDED → FAILED(VOIDED), on a SUCCEEDED charge → REFUNDED (full); `charge-back` → CHARGEBACK → SUSPENDED + FREE entitlement + M10; transaction type `representment` → CHARGEBACK_REPRESENTED (no state change). Dispute outcome has no documented API signal → OWNER-RUN command `pnpm billing:dispute --charge <ref> --outcome won|lost`: won → CHARGEBACK_RESOLVED + RESUMED (+ entitlement back); lost → ENDED(DISPUTE). No renewals while SUSPENDED. New charge_event kinds: `SUBMITTED`, `SUBMIT_UNKNOWN`, `REFUND_REQUESTED`, `CHARGEBACK_REPRESENTED`; new subscription events: `RENEWAL_NOTICE_SENT`; EndedCause adds `DISPUTE`. Affects P1, P2, P9, P14, P16 (CLI next to tax summary).

A10 (reconciliation windows). RESOLUTION: the daily reconciler runs three queries: `dateType=creation` last 3 days; `dateType=charge-back` last 120 days; `dateType=refund` last 120 days; plus the SUBMIT_UNKNOWN adoption check (A2). Affects P3 (params), P14.

A11 (CSP for the card form). RESOLUTION: the SDK `<script>` tag carries the page nonce (the policy is `'nonce-…' 'strict-dynamic'`, so host sources in script-src are ignored by CSP3 browsers); `frame-src` and `connect-src` get the xMoney origins; `form-action` and Caddy's `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` are MEASURED in X0 (3-D Secure may run in the SDK's modal iframe; if pop-ups are needed, only the card routes get `same-origin-allow-popups`, via a Caddy path matcher). The loosened policy applies ONLY to `/checkout`, `/checkout/return` and a dedicated `/settings/card` page — never to `/settings` itself (which holds account deletion and 2-step settings). Affects P19, P20, P22, X0.

A12 (card change). `verifyCard` is not an xMoney mode (enum auth|authAndCapture|credit). RESOLUTION (owner asked separately; default = temporary hold): card change = a new `managed` order through the embedded form with `cardTransactionMode: "auth"` and amount 1.00 USD, then the authorization is released with `DELETE /transaction/{id}` (a refund of an uncaptured auth = void). The new order becomes the subscription's `xmoney_order_id`. Exact behaviour confirmed in X0; if xMoney confirms amount 0 is allowed with `auth`, X0's recording switches the amount to 0. Affects P3 (`XMoneyEmbeddedOrder.cardTransactionMode: "authAndCapture" | "auth"`), P12, P20.

A13 (the fingerprinted serve file). `packages/serve/src/index.ts` is not frozen: its digest is sealed as the register row `serveContractHash` (apps/runner/src/dev-deployment-register.ts:535-555); dev has edited it several times, each time needing a new register version. RESOLUTION: Parts 1–2 do not touch it. S1 (scorecard merge) brings the scorecard's edits and therefore a new register version: the dev seeder recomputes it automatically; the hosted runbook gains "publish a new register version (serveContractHash) at this merge". Same rule for `packages/propagation/src/index.ts` (`propagationContractHash`). Affects S1, B11/P22 runbook.

A14 (Part 1a does not wait for billing). RESOLUTION: acceptance records run in every mode (records key required always); the country gate runs whenever hosted AND a `countryPolicy` row is published at the register version (absent row = no gate); both are independent of `billingPolicy.enabled`. The dev seeder publishes countryPolicy; the hosted example includes it. Affects L3, G2, G3, P22.

A15 (retention). Privacy Policy: acceptance records = life of the account + 6 years, then deleted; payment records = 10 years, then deleted. RESOLUTION: append-only tables get ONE sanctioned delete path: SECURITY DEFINER functions `legal.purge_expired_acceptance(now timestamptz)` and `billing.purge_expired_records(now timestamptz)`; the reject_mutation trigger is replaced on these tables by a guard that allows DELETE only when `current_setting('debateai.retention_purge', true) = 'on'`, which only those functions set (SET LOCAL). Acceptance rows are purgeable when the owner's account was erased more than 6 years ago (via `identity.account_erasure_request` completion time, which survives erasure) or, if never erased, never; billing rows when older than 10 full calendar years after the year of the charge. A yearly job calls them (built now, tested with a fake clock). Affects L3 (0077 guard + function), P1 (0080–0082 guards + function), P16 (job wiring).

A16 (routes/fields). Already in the contract: `scope` + `plan_id` on the room read AND on the 202 WAITING answer (`AskAcceptedSchema` gains `waiting_scope`), `GET /v1/billing/usage`, `GET /v1/billing/invoices`. Affects B6, B7, P12.

A17 (SmartBill duplicates + partial refunds). RESOLUTION: (a) `billing.invoice_intent (charge_id, kind, issuer, requested_at)` UNIQUE (charge_id, kind) written before any issuer call; (b) a timed-out/unknown SmartBill call is NEVER blindly retried: if SmartBill offers a lookup by our reference (X1 confirms: e.g. invoice "mentions"/observations carrying the charge id, or a list endpoint), look up first; if no lookup exists, mark `INVOICE_UNKNOWN` and list it in the owner summary for manual check; (c) a partial refund issues a partial credit invoice (negative line for the refunded amount referencing the original), not a whole-invoice storno; a full refund may use storno. X1 confirms the endpoints. Affects P1, P5, P10, P16.

A18 (step-up purpose). No authPolicy row holds step-up purposes; they are the CHECK constraint `step_up_grant_action_check` (migrations/0040:3434-3440). RESOLUTION: `0082_billing_outbox_cancel.sql` also replaces that CHECK to add `WITHDRAW_SUBSCRIPTION` (target_run_id NULL, target_account_id = user_id), mirroring DELETE_ACCOUNT; the API's step-up route learns the new action. Affects P1, P12.

A19 (outbox mutability). Variant (c) is `reject_delete` + column-level UPDATE grants (0065:119-135). RESOLUTION: `billing.outbox` = reject_delete trigger + truncate guard + `GRANT UPDATE (claimed_by, claimed_at, attempts, not_before, done_at, dead_at, last_error_code)` only. Affects P1, P7.

A20 (runner reads). The runner reads exactly: `billing.run_charge_scope`, `billing.person_windows_v` (SELECT grants), the `billingPlans` and `costEnvelopePolicy` register rows, and `@debateai/billing-core` (pure). Nothing else in `billing.`. Affects B5, B9.

A21 (no late-filled columns in append-only tables). RESOLUTION: drop `billing.customer.quaderno_contact_id`; the customer's locale lives in the profile events; e-Factura status → `billing.invoice_status_event (invoice_id, at, efactura_status)`; notice processing → `billing.xmoney_notice_outcome (notice_id, at, outcome)`. Affects P1, P9, P10.

A22 (one source per setting). RESOLUTION: remove `xmoney_environment` and `owner_report_email_ref` from `billingPolicy` (the environment follows `XMONEY_API_BASE_URL`; the owner's address is `OWNER_REPORT_EMAIL_PATH`); `sdk_environment` in the checkout response is derived from the base URL host (`api-stage.` → "stage"). The billing group of the environment is validated AFTER the register is read (boot step, `BILLING_CONFIGURATION_INCOMPLETE`); billing enabled additionally REQUIRES the three budget members in `costEnvelopePolicy` (`BILLING_REQUIRES_ENVELOPE_MEMBERS`). Affects B4, P6, P8.

A23 (key loading). RESOLUTION: the xMoney private key is loaded as BYTES (new crypto helper `readCustodyTextSecretBytes(path): Buffer` — one printable line, trimmed, held and zeroed through boot.hold) because it is both the HMAC key and the AES key source; Quaderno's key and SmartBill's `user:token` are text credentials loaded with the existing `readCustodyAuthorizationHeader` precedent (strings, like provider keys). Contract §6 functions take `privateKey: Buffer`. Affects L1 (helper) or P6, P3.

A24 (xMoney field names). `GET /card/{id}` requires `customerId` (already in the contract); server-side REST uses `orderType` (we do not create orders server-side except none — embedded payload uses the SDK's `order.type`, pinned by X0 test vectors); `charge_id` = 32 lower-case hex. Affects P3, X0.

A25 (cancel links). RESOLUTION: M3/M4/M7 link to the `/cancel` page (which asks for the email and sends a fresh one-time link), never to a token; token links open a page that needs a button click (POST) — mail scanners only GET; `billingCancelLink` is limited per IP (5/h) AND per account (3 per 24 h, keyed by the blind index, silent when exceeded). Affects P13, P17, P21.

A26 (build + mail). (a) `tools/orphan-audit/src/index.ts` package graph (~9-54) gains rows for the 7 new packages (each package's own task adds its row); (b) M2 carries a LINK to Quaderno's hosted PDF (non-RO) and ATTACHES the SmartBill PDF (RO, fetched via the SmartBill API); M1 attaches the accepted Terms as text; `TemplatedMailSender` sends multipart/mixed with text + html + attachments. Affects every new-package task, P10, P17.


## Appendix D — Rulings Q-1 to Q-16 (binding; wins over A–C)


- **Q-1 Outage at renewal (OWNER RULING).** When xMoney or the tax service is unavailable at a renewal (XMONEY_UNAVAILABLE, TAX_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, or a rebill outcome still unknown), the plan stays ACTIVE and the renewal is retried quietly for up to **3 days** (72 h from the period end): no charge without a fresh quote, no "payment failed" email, a new entitlement cause `RENEWAL_PENDING` extends `paid_through` by up to 72 h. After 72 h without an outcome, the normal dunning path starts (PAST_DUE, retries +1/+3/+7 days with M5A–C). Owners: B5 (cause + CHECK), P11a/P11b (logic + tests), P2 (fold, if it needs the cause).
- **Q-2 Notice answers.** `POST /v1/billing/xmoney/notify` answers 200 `OK` after the notice is stored; it answers 429 when the source is over its admission budget and 500 when the store write fails, so xMoney re-sends. The plan header's Global Constraint is amended to say exactly this.
- **Q-3 Terms archive.** Every published Terms/Privacy version is archived by sha256 at `apps/ui/legal/archive/<locale>/<sha256>.md` (the Terms promise "Previous versions at dezbatere.ro/terms/versions"); L2's generator writes the archive entry for each current document and the manifest maps sha256 → archive path; M1 attaches the ACCEPTED version from the archive (L3a's widened `latest()` returns its sha256). Owners: L2 (archive + manifest), L3a (latest returns sha256 + locale), P17 (resolver reads the archive), P9b (passes it).
- **Q-4 M7 link.** M7 (cancel confirmation) links to Settings, because only Settings can undo; M3/M4 link to the `/cancel` page (A25 stands for them).
- **Q-5 Owner alert for a dead refund.** Add owner template `O2` (English only): "A refund could not be completed and needs your attention" with charge ref, amount, reason code; RefundDesk's dead-letter path enqueues it to the owner address immediately. R-8's id list gains `O2`. Owners: P17 (template), P9b/RefundDesk (enqueue).
- **Q-6 Withdrawal window.** 14 **calendar** days from the first activation, in the customer's tax-country calendar day end (no public-holiday table). Business days are used only for xMoney's notice rules.
- **Q-7 Downgrade price.** The downgrade confirm shows the lower plan's net price from `GET /v1/billing/plans` with "+ tax, from {date}"; no downgrade-quote route.
- **Q-8 /new plan chooser.** With billing on, the Free/Premium chooser is hidden; the page shows the person's plan name and the server decides the tier (B10a owns this).
- **Q-9 Owner withdrawal command.** `pnpm billing:withdraw --owner <ref>` runs P12d's withdrawal for a request received by email (the Terms allow "write to support@"); owner-run, audited. Owner: P12d (D6b).
- **Q-10 Legal accept gate.** The UI gate fails open when the status check fails; the server's billing refusal (`LEGAL_REACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`) is the real guard. Accepted.
- **Q-11 Waker hold.** The waker opens its hold with the B2 estimator; S2 does not re-pick at wake time (known limit, listed).
- **Q-12 Records key escrow.** The records key is backed up as a sixth escrowed secret in the existing backup envelope (owner confirms in the runbook step).
- **Q-13 Admission keys.** Source-keyed billing scopes (`billingNotify`, `billingCancelLink`) use `clientIpNetworkScope(source.ip)` like G3a; owner-keyed `billingQuote` stays owner-keyed.
- **Q-14 Migration list.** Header R1 reads: legal 0077, budget 0078, billing 0079–0084, scorecard 0085. Every migration task appends its file to `tests/architecture/security-migration-0065.test.ts`'s pinned list in build order (L3a 0077 first).
- **Q-15 Shipped-corpus manifest.** Every task that creates a shipped source file runs the shipped-corpus manifest check (`tests/support/shipped-corpus.manifest.txt`) the way D6a does and lists the manifest in its Files/git add.
- **Q-16 Scaffold/edge pins.** Every new-package task (L2, G1, B4b, P3a, P4, P5, P17) adds its row to `tests/architecture/scaffold.test.ts` and the orphan-audit package graph, measuring the pinned count first.

companion rule `assertAddedMountsAfterRegion` (`tests/support/zone-boundary.ts:399-403`: a new `api.get/post(…)` mount
must sit AFTER the region) checks nothing today — `assertZoneBoundaryIntact` passes a repository-root path to
`git diff` from the `dialectical-engine/` cwd, so the diff is always empty (the age gate's two age-confirmation mounts
at `:1880` and `:1888` sit before the region and pass) — but its intent is honoured here: every route
this part mounts (L4's two, G3a's one) goes AFTER the region, directly after the age gate's `POST /v1/auth/age-check`
block (`:2138-2152`), so they stay legal when that check is repaired (Open question 11).

#### Asks of later tasks (for the assembler)

These follow from the rulings; each names the task that must honour it.
- **P6a (D5):** consumes L1's `readCustodyTextSecretBytes` from `@debateai/crypto` and deletes its own definition (R-6); its A23 test either goes (L1's `tests/unit/records-key.test.ts` covers the helper) or uses L1's codes — `SECRET_TEXT_ABSENT` for a missing file, `SECRET_TEXT_INVALID` for two lines or a blank file, `SECRET_CUSTODY_INVALID` for loose custody — and L1's trimming (surrounding spaces are trimmed, not refused).
- **P8a (D6a):** the billing legal gate asks L4's `legal.requiresReacceptance(ownerRef)` (the `legal` binding in `main.ts`), e.g. `{ mustReaccept: (ownerRef) => legal.requiresReacceptance(ownerRef) }`, and defines no second floor rule (D6a's current text already does this).
- **B3 (D2), B5 (D3) — R3-1:** L3a writes `"0079_legal_acceptance.sql"` as the pinned list's LAST entry with no trailing comma, directly after dev's `"0077_age_gate.sql"` (or the colleague's `"0078_sensitive_data_consent.sql"` once merged); B3 gives it the comma and appends `0080_budget_holds_waiting_line.sql`, B5 appends `0081_billing_entitlement.sql` and adds `"billing"` (second, after `"audit_crypto_internal"`) to the P3-01 `ownsSchemas` and its pinned literal. D2's and D3's current texts already say exactly this.
- **P8c (D6a):** consumes L2's `CONSENT_KEYS`, `consentDocument` and `buildConsentManifestEntries` from `apps/ui/scripts/legal-consent-manifest.mjs` and creates neither that file nor its test; the generator already merges the consent entries (`buildLegalManifest(readDraft, consentEntries)`), so P8c's "merge into `documents[locale]`" step goes, and so do its edits of `apps/ui/scripts/generate-legal-data.mjs` / `.d.mts` (`main` already passes `buildConsentManifestEntries(...)` as the second argument). P8c also drops its "Modify `packages/legal-manifest/src/index.ts` (L2's `parseManifest`)" step: L2 has no `parseManifest` and no `VERSION` constant — its parser is `parseLegalManifest(value)`, which already admits exactly `sha256-<first 12 hex of the pair's sha256>` for the two consent kinds and `N.M` for the documents (`validPair`, per kind). Where P8c needs a parser it imports `parseLegalManifest`. Its checkout rows keep `kind: "RENEWAL_TERMS" | "IMMEDIATE_START"`, `surface: "CHECKOUT"` and the manifest's `sha256-…` versions, which 0079's `acceptance_document_version_shape` admits.
- **P8c, P15 (D6a, D6b):** acceptance evidence is sealed with L3b's `sealAcceptanceEvidence(recordsKey, acceptanceId, {ip, userAgent})` from `apps/api/src/legal.ts`, bound to each row's own `acceptanceId` (not the owner ref, not `user_agent`).
- **P16c (D6b):** calls `SELECT legal.purge_expired_acceptance($1::timestamptz) AS purged` as `debateai_runtime` (granted in 0079); the result is a `bigint` row count — the rows deleted from `legal.acceptance` AND `legal.account_closure` together (the audit field D6b names `acceptances` then counts both; no code change needed).
- **P9a, P13 (D6a, D6b) — ruling Q-13:** the source-keyed billing scopes `billingNotify` and `billingCancelLink` admit by `clientIpNetworkScope(source.ip)` (`apps/api/src/client-ip.ts:49`), as G3a's `geoAvailability` does — never the raw address (DL5-F3: one IPv6 /64 would otherwise walk every per-IP window and fill the scope's key table). P8b's `billingQuote` stays owner-keyed (Q-13), so it passes the owner ref, not an address.
- **P23 (D7) and M1 (D6a):** in hosted mode (`owedWithoutRecord: true`, which `main.ts` passes when `DEPLOYMENT_MODE === "hosted"`) L4 owes both documents to any account with NO acceptance row, whatever the floor; in local mode only a set floor does. An account created directly in a hosted test stack (no sign-up rows) is therefore sent to the accept screen on `/new` and `/debate`, and the billing gate refuses it. A task that composes `RepositoryLegalAcceptanceApplication` itself must pass `owedWithoutRecord` (it is required). D7's stubbed gate comment (`legal: { requiresReacceptance: async () => false }`) should give THAT as the reason: "the stack's accounts are made active directly and hold no acceptance rows, which L4 would otherwise send to the accept screen (L4's own suites own that rule)" — not that the gate answers "nothing to accept again". Under ruling Q-3, M1 attaches the ACCEPTED version, not the current one: D6a's P9b passes the fields of the newest TERMS row (`documentSha256`, `locale`, `documentVersion` from L3a's `latest()`), and no comment in D6a should say "the current Terms of the person's locale ARE the accepted version" (D1's earlier wording request is withdrawn).
- **P18 (D7):** writes `billing.consent.renewal` and `billing.consent.immediateStart` into all 35 `billing.json` files together (one without the other stops the generator), then runs `pnpm run generate:legal` and commits `packages/legal-manifest/src/manifest.json` (R-27).
- **P18, P19 (D7):** `GET /v1/geo/availability`'s `pay` is the country rule only; the UI offers paying only when it is true AND the billing routes answer (a 404 from `GET /v1/billing/plans` means billing is off).
- **P19, P21 (D7):** `@debateai/legal-manifest` is already in `apps/ui/package.json` and `transpilePackages` (L2); they add neither again.
- **P23 (D7):** composes `new RegistrationService({ ..., legalAcceptance: { recordsKey } })`; there is no `acceptance` repository option (the rows travel inside `createPendingAccount`). A registration driven through `buildApi` needs, since PR #41, a real adult `date_of_birth` in the body (the age gate's hook turns it into `adult_affirmed`) and, with the records key composed, the `terms`, `privacy` and `locale` members beside it; a direct `service.register(input, source)` call passes the pairs on the SOURCE (`RegistrationSource.legal`), because `RegisterInput` has no `legal` member (the frozen S04 register mount builds it from four body members). The contract client is `register(email, password, recoveryEmail, dateOfBirth, legal)`.
- **Whoever merges `feat/sensitive-data-consent` after L2 (R3-7):** that branch rewrites two sentences in all 70 legal drafts (their `Version` lines unchanged), so the merge commit runs `pnpm generate:legal` and commits the new archive files and `packages/legal-manifest/src/manifest.json` (L2 Step 5, "Later merges"); `TERMS_VERSIONS` needs no new row (same version, a second archived text).
- **B4a, P16, S1a:** each moves the `register-support-publication` row-count pins by measuring first, after G2's +1 (R-18).
- **B4b (D3), P3a/P4/P5 (D5), P17 (D7), S1a (D8):** `tests/architecture/scaffold.test.ts`'s edge-row pin leaves Part 1a at **30** (L2 28 -> 29, G1 29 -> 30, each measured first, each with its own `// N -> N+1: the <pkg> package row (A26(a)).` line above the `it`, the `it(` title and `toBe(N)` moved together). Each later package task continues the same way (B4b 30 -> 31, P3a/P4/P5 31 -> 34, P17 34 -> 35), and D8's S1a conflict row 24 adds only the scorecard's own rows on top of the count measured on the merged tree.
- **P9b (D6a), P17 (D7) — ruling Q-3:** P9b reads the accepted Terms from L3a's widened `acceptances.latest(ownerRef, "TERMS")` — `{documentVersion, documentSha256, locale, acceptedAt} | null`, all from the newest row — and carries `sha256` and `locale` (and `version`) into the M1 job fields. adds the pairs after `dateOfBirth`, L4's screen comes after the age interstitial), and the `/terms/versions` page (R3-4:
L2 decided — the editorial list stays, the archive decides its membership by a test). Closed by D6a's reading: the
country pre-fill at checkout (D7's P19 sends its first quote without a country, so no `CountryGate.countryHint` is built).
Closed by D7's reading (round 3): D7's ask that every archived Terms row of `/terms/versions` link to
`/terms/versions/<sha256>` (P21's page) is what L2's "archive agree" test already pins (Asks, P21), and D7's P21 builds
`/privacy/versions` straight over `legalArchive("PRIVACY", locale)`, so no second Privacy list exists to pin; which
archived texts those lists show (pre-go-live drafts included) stays D7's Open question 3 for the owner or counsel, with
this list's question 9 as its cause.

1. **A15's erasure clock (recorded choice, owner may still object).** A15 names `identity.account_erasure_request`'s completion time; that table keeps no `owner_ref` and its `user_id` is `SET NULL` by the delete that ends the account (0040:793). L3a dates closure with an `AFTER DELETE` trigger on `identity."user"` into `legal.account_closure` (the only delete of that table is `identity.finalize_account_erasure`, 0040:5829). Same rule, a date that can be found; the reconciliation accepted the table.
2. **`lookupRegion` (spec §2.3.3, Ukraine) — built, answering no region.** G1 defines `lookupRegion` on the lookup object (`RegionLookup`, returned beside the contract's `GeoLookup`), with `region: null` until a DB-IP *city* file is configured; nothing downloads one and nothing calls it. Opening Ukraine is then: add the city file to G4's refresh, fill `region`, and block the occupied regions.
3. **Reason words for the always-blocked list.** RU, BY, KP → `SANCTIONS`; CN, HK, MO, IR, CU, SY, VE, VN → `PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED` (Cuba and Iran deliberately not "sanctions", per the EU Blocking Statute note in spec §2.12 item 7). The colleague/lawyer may prefer other words; the switches are the same either way.
4. **English fallback at sign-up (owner ruling needed — a deviation from spec §2.3.2).** The spec refuses "when either pair is not the manifest's current pair for that locale". L3b's `resolveDocument` also accepts the current ENGLISH pair for any locale and records the row with locale `"en"`, because `useLegalDocument` shows the English document when a locale's chunk fails to load, and the record should say what was on screen. The alternative is to drop the fallback: the UI sends the pair of the document actually displayed with that document's locale, and the server refuses a locale mismatch with `LEGAL_DOCUMENT_STALE` (the person reloads). Either is one line in `resolveDocument` plus its test. (With Q-3's archive, the English row's text is attachable either way: `archivedDocument("TERMS", "en", sha256)`.)
5. **No record = owed, in hosted mode only (recorded choice; owner may prefer the literal reading everywhere).** The rule depends on the mode, passed in explicitly as `owedWithoutRecord: environment.DEPLOYMENT_MODE === "hosted"` (`apps/api/src/main.ts`).
   - **Local mode: the literal spec rule.** "none, unless the manifest's marker moved past their last acceptance" (§2.3.2), and "Local mode keeps today's behaviour exactly" (§2.2 rule 1). An account with no record sees no accept screen until the owners set a floor, and `accept` writes nothing for it. The billing reason for the stricter rule (subscribing with no Terms record, so M1 has no accepted version to attach) does not exist there: local mode has no billing routes. A14 moves only the sign-up WRITE into every mode, so new local accounts still get their records.
   - **Hosted mode: every account without a record accepts once.** Every account created before L3b sees the accept screen once on `/new` and `/debate` (never on `/settings`) and cannot subscribe until it accepts, so every subscriber has a Terms record for M1 to attach.
   - **The owner's alternative.** To use the literal rule in both modes, `main.ts` passes `owedWithoutRecord: false` in hosted mode too (one line in `main.ts` plus the composition case's pinned string in `tests/unit/legal-reacceptance.test.ts`; L4's local-mode case already covers the behaviour). Hosted accounts created before L3b could then subscribe with no Terms record, and M1 would have no accepted version to attach for them.
6. **Admission on `POST /v1/account/legal-accept` (for the next sealed `ADMISSION_POLICY` version).** The route writes only what is owed, so repeated calls add nothing; it still costs a status read per call. INTERFACE-CONTRACT §4 fixes this program's new admission scopes, so no owner-keyed `legalAccept` scope is added here; decide whether the next sealed admission version should carry one.
7. **The ADULT acceptance row beside the age gate's record (recorded choice; owner or counsel may drop it).** Spec §2.3.2 writes `ADULT`, `TERMS` and `PRIVACY_SHOWN` at sign-up, and L3a keeps all three. Since PR #41 the account also carries `identity.age_check` (the passed check, its rule version and country), but that row belongs to the account (`ON DELETE CASCADE`) and goes with it at erasure; the `ADULT` row, under the Terms pair that states the minimum age and sealed under the records key, is the one proof of the affirmation that survives the erasure for the six-year retention. Dropping it is two lines (the kind list in `signUpAcceptanceRows` and the wrapper's `ARRAY['ADULT','PRIVACY_SHOWN','TERMS']` check) plus their tests.
8. **`cf-ipcountry` from a client (for P22's Caddy rules; owner).** The age gate records `cf-ipcountry` whenever a request carries it (`edgeCountry`, kept by R3-3). Behind Caddy with no Cloudflare that header can only come from the client itself; the UI's `/api` proxy drops it (`apps/ui/app/api/[...path]/route.ts:14-31` does not list it), so browsers going through the UI are recorded with the gate's DB-IP country, but a request that reaches the API port directly with a forged header would be recorded with the forged country (never decisive — nothing refuses or allows on it). If the hosted Caddyfile can reach the API without the UI, P22 should strip the header there (`request_header -Cf-Ipcountry`); nothing in Part 1a relies on it.
9. **Archive growth before go-live (Q-3, recorded choice).** Every edit of a draft — a counsel change, a translation fix — adds one archive file on the next `pnpm generate:legal`, even when the draft keeps its `Version N.M`; nothing is ever pruned, because an acceptance row may name that exact hash. So one version may have several archived texts (the "previous versions" page lists them by version, then hash). If the owner wants every published text change to carry a new version number, the generator could refuse a new hash under an already-archived version of the same locale; that is not built, because each translation fix would then need a version bump in all 35 locales (the locale check pins every locale's version to English's).
10. **Which refusal a person meets first (recorded choice; owner may reorder).** On `POST /v1/auth/register` G3a's country refusal runs BEFORE the age gate's hook, so a closed country is told "not available in your country" whatever date was typed, and no 30-day age lockout is ever set for a place that could not sign up anyway (the sign-up page already shows G1 instead of the form there). On `POST /v1/asks`, once `feat/sensitive-data-consent` merges, its consent check sits above admission and the country refusal below it (G3a Step 5), so a person in an always-blocked place who never consented is first asked to consent and then told new debates cannot start from there. Putting the country refusal first in the ask path too is a two-line move inside the colleague's new block; it was not made, to leave that code as written.
11. **The S04 zone's containment rule checks nothing today (a finding for the owner; nothing in Part 1a depends on it).** `assertZoneBoundaryIntact` (`tests/support/zone-boundary.ts:432-481`) runs `git diff --unified=0 <base> -- <path>` with `cwd` = `dialectical-engine/` but a path relative to the REPOSITORY root (`dialectical-engine/apps/api/src/index.ts`), which git resolves under the cwd and finds nothing; so `assertAddedMountsAfterRegion` (`:399-403`) always sees an empty diff (measured: the age gate's mounts at `:1880` and `:1888`, before the region, pass). The live half — the region's content hash, `ZONE_REGION_MODIFIED` — does work, and it is what forced L3b's and G3a's hooks. This part mounts every new route after the region anyway (Part intro), so a repair of the pathspec (`relative(options.repoRoot, indexPath)`, or `cwd: gitRoot`) would stay green for it; the age gate's two age-confirmation mounts would then need moving. Not fixed here (fragment edits only, no task chips).
12. **`age_frozen` and the acceptance record (for the record).** A frozen account keeps its `legal.acceptance` rows (nothing deletes them but the six-year purge after an erasure) and cannot sign in, so it never sees L4's screen or reaches the country gate. If the owner later adds an "unfreeze" path, that account's rows are simply still there.

- **Why a run waits is recorded, not re-derived by walking the line.** With billing on, a Free person whose month
  is FULL waits until it resets (A5: only FULL waits), up to a month, so such runs pile up at the head of the line.
  Budget spec §2.3 rule 1: "a run waiting only because its own person's allowance is full never holds anyone else
  back". Walking the line per ask (five reads per run, under the site-wide day lock) and capping the walk (a capped
  walk must answer "blocking") would let a few hundred Free accounts stall every new question and starve the waker.
  So each wait records WHY it waits (`core.run_wait_reason`, B3: `SITE` or `PERSON` with the instant the person's
  own block can first lift), the ask asks the line ONE indexed question (B6a), and the waker reads only the runs
  worth trying, page by page (B7b). A person's windows cannot be computed in SQL (`billing.person_windows_v`,
  B5, exposes the entitlement in force, not the windows: those are `personWindowsFor` in TypeScript), so the
  classification is made once, by the same `decideRoom` code that decides the admission, and re-made when it can
  have changed: at the recorded instant, after an entitlement event, at boot, and at least hourly.

#### Open questions (for the assembler)

- **Switching the band off while questions wait — refused in code; drain step only if the owner asks.** A later register version without the band builds no room and no waker, so B6b's `ask-room` boot step refuses that boot with `WAITING_LINE_REQUIRES_BAND` while `core.run_waiting_v` lists any run, and `readRun` refuses a WAITING run with no room by the same name. D3's B11b runbook ("Removing them again") now says exactly this and keeps the operator's `SELECT count(*) FROM core.run_waiting_v` check. Still open for the owner: keep the refusal (default), or ask for a drain step instead (record each waiting run FAILED `RUN_SETUP_FAILED:WAITING_LINE` before such a version is published).
- **PLAN_CHANGED — the end state of a stranded premium question (owner question, narrowed by RULINGS-R2 Q-11).** A waiting premium question whose owner's plan has dropped to Free by the time room frees up (period-end cancel, withdrawal, dunning end, chargeback suspension, a lapse past `paid_through` — including one after Q-1's up-to-72 h `RENEWAL_PENDING` extension runs out) is recorded FAILED `RUN_SETUP_FAILED:PLAN_CHANGED` ("ask again under your current plan"), not started on the paid roster under a Free charge scope (the Free 110% wall does not bound the first position's call or the answer, budget spec §2.9). RULINGS-R2 Q-11 rules out a re-pick at wake time, so re-picking the run at ECONOMY under the Free cap is closed. The one remaining alternative is to start it as CLOSE on the paid roster under the Free charge scope with the B9 wall — not the default for the reason above. Default FAILED until the owner rules otherwise; a move between paid plans, and Free → paid, still start. D8's S2 lists the same case among its Q-11 known limits ("a plan change before the wake", settled by this `PLAN_CHANGED`) and agrees that nothing runs under Free's windows on a premium pin; D3's B8 stores a swapped question that waits on its plan's own ask, so the check sees it as premium.
- **`apps/api`'s manifest edge for `@debateai/billing-core` (for the assembler).** B6b imports `BillingPersonAllowanceSource` from `@debateai/billing-core` through the root devDependency B4b added, and changes neither `apps/api/package.json` nor the `apps/api` row of `tools/orphan-audit/src/index.ts` — the `@debateai/budget` precedent (`apps/api/src/main.ts:45` imports it with no manifest entry), R-1's wording, and D5's P6a, which adds `billing-core` to that manifest and row together with the three connector packages and says B6b edits neither. D3 and D4 asked B6b to add the edge now instead. If the assembler prefers the edge declared at first import, B6b's Step 5 gains `"@debateai/billing-core":"workspace:*"` in `apps/api/package.json` `dependencies` (sorted after `@debateai/battery`), `"billing-core"` appended to the `apps/api` row's allowed list, a `pnpm install` (lockfile importers only) and `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `apps/api/package.json` and `tools/orphan-audit/src/index.ts` in its `git add`; P6a's "keep any of the four already present" rule already tolerates that.
- **Why a run waits is re-measured, not walked.** A PERSON reason is looked at again at its `person_recheck_at` (the latest reset among the windows full on spend alone, or the next tick when only the person's own live holds fill them), after an entitlement event it was not measured with, at every process start (the first full sweep), and at least hourly (the backstop for time-driven changes such as a lapse past `paid_through`). Between those instants a person-blocked run is neither a waker candidate nor a line-blocker. A tick that must re-measure many PERSON runs at once (the boot sweep, or an hour after it) is long; the single-flight trigger then skips a minute rather than overlapping. No per-tick time budget is added; owner to confirm.
- **Serialisation cost, accepted for now.** The room decision holds the site's day lock across the run's creation (key provisioning, the memory question, the hold and the first job) so the hold commits with the job; asks are serialised site-wide for that span. The first job is queued last, on the decision's transaction, so the one shared sequence row it takes is held only until that commit. Provider discovery runs outside the lock (between the precheck and the decision). One API instance in production (spec §2.14 item 5). The line's own cost under the lock is now one statement, whatever its length.
- **Holds opened before a UTC day end count on that day.** `readSiteCountedHoldsMicros(day)` counts every live hold opened no later than the end of `day` — a run started before midnight and still running counts its unspent hold against the new day too (the careful side). Owner to confirm.
- **A waiting run with no `plan_tier`** (none is created that way by this program) is estimated as `premium`, the careful side, and is therefore also refused by the PLAN_CHANGED check for an owner on Free.
- **The usage bars show spend only**, not holds (`usagePercent`), so a bar can read below 100% while a running debate's hold makes the window FULL for a new question; sentences P1–P3 come from the room read, not the bars. Owner to confirm at the look gate.
- **`RoomPreview.waitReason` — one fixture outside this fragment must follow (for the assembler).** B6a's `RoomPreview` now has the required member `waitReason: WaitReason` (D8's Open question 11: S2 plans a waiting question for `waitReason.personRecheckAt`, and without it cannot tell a wait on the person's own live holds from a wait on spend); `precheck` returns `evaluation.waitReason`, and B6b's `PREVIEW` carries `{ waitsFor: "SITE", personRecheckAt: null }`. D8's S1a room double and S2's preview helpers already carry it. D3's B8 unit test does not yet: in `tests/unit/b8-server-plan.test.ts`, `recordingRoom`'s `precheck` returns `{ admission, estimateMicros: 1_000, now: NOW, personUses: [] }`, which no longer typechecks, and must return `{ admission, estimateMicros: 1_000, now: NOW, personUses: [], waitReason: Object.freeze({ waitsFor: "SITE", personRecheckAt: null }) }` — the exact line D3's own Open question 13 gives. Apply both in the same assembly, or the root typecheck turns red at B8.
- **A waiting run whose owner is suspended or age-frozen rests in line indefinitely (owner to confirm; RULINGS-R3 R3-2).** `core.run_waiting_v` keeps only `state = 'active'` owners, so such a run is neither woken nor holding anyone back, holds no money (a waiting run has no hold) and is back in line, unchanged, if the account becomes `active` again (B3's integration test proves both for `suspended` and 0077's `age_frozen`); erasure deletes the account row and so drops it for good. An account the age interstitial refused is frozen for good in practice (dev's 0077 revokes every session and no path un-freezes it), so its waiting run is never started and never failed: it stays a `run_wait` row with no FAILED job, invisible to the line, the waker, `countWaiting()` and the owner (who cannot sign in). Default: leave it resting (nothing written, nothing lost, the same rule as a suspended account). The alternative, if the owner prefers a closed record: B7b's waker records FAILED `RUN_SETUP_FAILED:ACCOUNT_INACTIVE` for a waiting run whose owner is `age_frozen` — not built.
- **The consent gate is assumed to stay in the HTTP handler (for the assembler; RULINGS-R3 R3-6).** On `feat/sensitive-data-consent` (ae6c1d0d) the refusal is the first statement of `POST /v1/asks`, so `submit` — and the whole room — is behind it; B6b's Step 6b proves it once the branch has merged. If the colleague moves the check into `submit` or `evaluateAskAdmission` before merging, it must stay ahead of `#submitWithRoom`'s first statement (B6b's instruction says so), and D3's B8 — whose billing step sits in front of the room branch — must stay behind it too.

**The two source audits — how every task below runs them** (the D5 convention, stated here because Part 1b runs first). `pnpm run lint` is `pnpm run audit:architecture && pnpm run audit:source` (`package.json:17`). At dev afbfe5ad (re-measured: PRs #37–#42 add no package, no edge row, no `process.env` read outside the register loader and no numeric export the audit's pattern matches, so the baseline below is 24be86f5's) `audit:architecture` already exits 1 on dev's three F31 edges (`tools/orphan-audit/src/cli.ts:15-17` sets exit code 1 on any violation; `tests/architecture/scaffold.test.ts:34-38`; `tests/ci-known-red.txt:144`), so `lint` never reaches `audit:source`, and the rules on `process.env`, `switch` + `exhaustive(`, test imports and numeric exports would never run. So no step here runs `pnpm run lint`. Each runs `pnpm run typecheck`, then the two audits on their OWN Run lines, never joined with `&&`:
- `pnpm run typecheck`: **Expected:** exit 0.
- `pnpm run audit:architecture`: **Expected:** exit 1, and `"violations"` is exactly these three lines and nothing else: `apps/api -> obs-capture is not a declared edge`, `apps/runner -> obs-capture is not a declared edge`, `apps/scheduler -> obs-capture is not a declared edge`. There is no `dependency cycle reaches` line, no other `is not a declared edge` line and no `has no manifest` line. A new package row shows up only in `"edgeRowsChecked"`.
- `pnpm run audit:source`: **Expected:** exit 1, and `"blocking"` is exactly these three lines and nothing else (dev's baseline, pinned at `tests/architecture/scaffold.test.ts:69-75`): `packages/obs-capture/install/api.ts reads the process environment outside the register loader`, and the same line for `packages/obs-capture/install/runner.ts` and for `packages/obs-capture/install/scheduler.ts`. Any other line fails the step: a new `process.env` read, a `switch` without `default:` + `exhaustive(`, a test or fixture import, a numeric export, or a migration replay finding (`migrations/0081_billing_entitlement.sql`).

**The shipped-corpus oracle** (the D1/D2/D5/D6a convention). `tests/unit/s1-1-depth-contract.test.ts:372-398` walks `packages`, `apps` and `web` (`:298-300`: extensions `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts` and `.mjs`; `node_modules`, `generated`, `.next`, `dist`, `build` and `__tests__` skipped). It turns red on any file not listed in `tests/support/shipped-corpus.manifest.txt`, naming it under `added`. So every task here that creates a shipped file adds it to the manifest in its own commit: B4a, B4b, B5, B8, B10a and B10c. That includes the UI's own `.test.mjs` files under `apps/ui`, which the scan reads too. B10b, B11a, B11b, B11c and B11d create no shipped file (tests, migrations, JSON and Markdown are outside the scan); B11d still runs the corpus test once on the merged tree, without the update variable, and expects the manifest unchanged. The step is the same in each task:
1. Run the corpus test and see it FAIL, naming exactly the task's new paths under `added` and nothing under `missing`.
2. Regenerate with `SHIPPED_CORPUS_MANIFEST_UPDATE=1` (`tests/support/shippedCorpusManifest.ts:71-74` rewrites the file sorted and keeps the header).
3. Read `git diff tests/support/shipped-corpus.manifest.txt`: only those added lines, and no removed line.
4. Run the test again without the variable and see it PASS.

This works only if every earlier task (D1's, B1–B3, B6a and B7a) kept the manifest in step the same way, so each expected diff here is exactly the task's own files.

4. **Clocks (resolved in code, for the record).** `EntitlementRepository.current(ownerRef, now)` resolves at the caller's `now`; `person_windows_v` (the runner's read, A20) resolves at the database's `statement_timestamp()`, while the runner takes its `now` from its own clock before the query. The two clocks can differ, and an anchor AFTER the caller's `now` is reachable three ways:
   - the view resolving at `statement_timestamp()` after the runner's `now`, when a period end or an API-dated event (a new subscription's activation instant) falls in that gap. A lapse anchors at `paid_through`, so a plan that lapses in the gap reads FREE anchored after the runner's `now`;
   - an event the API dates from its own clock while the reader's clock trails it;
   - an INITIAL charge anchored at xMoney's `transaction.createdAt`, a third clock.
   `computeWindows` refuses an instant before its anchor (`BILLING_WINDOW_BEFORE_ANCHOR`), which inside the runner's wall check would be an untyped refusal on an arguing call, against the budget rule that a run never ends FAILED for money. So `BillingPersonAllowanceSource.read` (used by both the API and the runner) builds the windows at max(now, anchor): a plan that began, or lapsed, just after `now` reads the windows that open at its anchor, with nothing spent in them yet. `computeWindows` keeps its refusal (it guards the pure function; B4b's test pins it). The runner stays on the view, as A20 requires. The lazy Free event reads `identity."user".created_at`, which `debateai_runtime` may still SELECT (0030:144-148; 0040 revoked only INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE).

It deliberately has no CHECK tying its `paid_through` to "period end + 72 h": the entitlement row does not carry the period end, and when P11a writes the row (at the period end, or at the first blocked attempt a few minutes before it) is P11a's decision. P11a's tests pin the bound; if the owner wants the database to enforce it too, P11a's shape must be fixed first (`effective_at` = the period end), and the CHECK becomes `cause <> 'RENEWAL_PENDING' OR paid_through <= effective_at + interval '72 hours'`, added to 0081 before it is built.

B7a's `GET /v1/asks/room`, which B8 routes through `decideRoomSettings`, and B7a's `GET /v1/billing/usage` are not asks, so with billing on a signed-in person who has not yet consented can read their room and usage. The only row either read writes is B5's lazy `SIGNED_UP_FREE` event (an owner reference, a plan id and instants: no question text, nothing sensitive), which that person's first ask would write anyway.
