- Behaviour to know (settled): only served-lane BODY debate calls are walled. The evaluator add-on's and the story's
  calls count toward the day's spend but are never walled mid-run (the story has its own cap, budget spec §2.6). The
  hosted runner always builds the wall; the band switches only its site-day half (and B9c's fallback, and B9d's
  check). The person half depends on the charge-scope row alone (R-19), never on the band: the runner builds
  `BillingPersonAllowanceSource` whenever `billingPlans` is sealed, even with billing off or without the band; that is
  harmless because B6 writes no charge-scope row while billing is off (R-19), so no run has a person scope and the only
  cost is one read by primary key per walled BODY call. A run WITH a charge scope on a runner whose register version
  lacks the band (version skew: billing on requires the band at the API's version, A22) is still held to the
  person's windows. When `billingPlans` is NOT sealed at the runner's register version (hosted, band or no band), the
  person wall fails closed: a run WITH a charge scope (admitted by an API that could read the plans) stops arguing with
  ALLOWANCE at its first walled call, and a run without one is untouched.

#### Hand-offs (owned by other tasks; B9 consumes or informs them)

Items 1–7 are carried by their owners' text (checked against D2, D3 and D8 at this revision); they are restated so a
reviewer of B9 can check the names without opening the other fragments. Item 7 was the last wording change asked of
another fragment (D8); D8 has applied it, and it changed no code. Item 8 is ruling R3-1's renumbering as it reaches
the names B9 reads from D2 and D3. No ask of another fragment remains open.

1. **B3 (R-20) — the stop CHECKs in `migrations/0080_budget_holds_waiting_line.sql`** (0078 before ruling R3-1). 0076 lets
   `body_stop`/`serve_stop` hold only `MONEY, ATTEMPTS, USAGE, DAILY(, TRANSPORT_DEATH, NO_ARTIFACT)`; a person's
   window writes `ALLOWANCE`, and a refused CHECK would lose the whole disclosure row. B3 carries this block (replay-safe
   with `DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS`; its `tests/architecture/b3-migration-0080.test.ts` (renamed from
   `b3-migration-0078.test.ts` with its migration under R3-1, which renames test names mentioning the number) and
   `tests/integration/b3-holds-waiting-line.test.ts` pin both constraint names):
   ```sql
   ALTER TABLE serve.serve_disclosure DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS serve_disclosure_body_stop_check;
   ALTER TABLE serve.serve_disclosure ADD CONSTRAINT serve_disclosure_body_stop_check
     CHECK (body_stop IS NULL OR body_stop IN ('MONEY', 'ATTEMPTS', 'USAGE', 'DAILY', 'ALLOWANCE'));
   ALTER TABLE serve.serve_disclosure DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS serve_disclosure_serve_stop_check;
   ALTER TABLE serve.serve_disclosure ADD CONSTRAINT serve_disclosure_serve_stop_check
     CHECK (serve_stop IS NULL OR serve_stop IN ('MONEY', 'ATTEMPTS', 'USAGE', 'DAILY', 'ALLOWANCE', 'TRANSPORT_DEATH', 'NO_ARTIFACT'));
   ```
   B9b's integration case "lets the owner's disclosure row name the person's allowance" proves it end to end.
2. **B8 (R-2) — `RunCostSubstitutionRepository` in `packages/db/src/run-cost-substitution.ts`.** B8 defines, and
   `@debateai/db` exports, `RUN_COST_SUBSTITUTION_REASONS`, `RunCostSubstitutionReason`, `RunCostSubstitutionInput
   {runId, callSiteKey, plannedProviderRef, usedProviderRef, reason, recordedAt: Date}` (all required),

`DOWNGRADED` switches the plan only (from ACTIVE or PAST_DUE) and the following `RENEWED`/`RECOVERED` moves the period

### Notes from part D6a

These tasks build the server half of paying: the durable job queue, the four checkout routes, the xMoney notice route
and the check that follows it, the one refund executor, the invoice jobs, and the monthly renewal with its failure
handling. They follow the contract (INTERFACE-CONTRACT.md) as amended by AMENDMENTS-R1 and by the assembler's
RECONCILE-DECISIONS (R-1 … R-39); the precedence is RULINGS-R3 (the rebase onto dev afbfe5ad, 29 September
evening), then RULINGS-R2 (the owner's and the assembler's rulings of 29 September), then AMENDMENTS-R1, then
RECONCILE-DECISIONS, then the contract.

**The R2 rulings built here:** Q-1 (an outage at a renewal keeps the plan for 72 hours: P11a, P11b), Q-2 (the notice
route's 200 / 429 / 500: P9a), Q-3 (M1 attaches the ACCEPTED Terms, which L2 archives by hash: P9b passes L3a's
`latest` hash and locale), Q-5 (the owner email `O2` for a refund that could not be completed: P7's id, P9b's
dead-letter path), Q-13 (source-keyed admissions by network, owner-keyed `billingQuote`: P8a, P9a) and Q-15 (the
shipped-corpus manifest step in every task that creates a shipped file, below).

**Built for D6b's round-2 findings:** P9c gives a second refund made elsewhere a durable mark D6b's P16b can list
(its VERIFY_PAYMENT job ends DEAD `REFUND_UNRECORDED`, D6b's 1(b)); P11a's cancel note says a cancel after the
renewal's `REQUESTED` ends the plan and counts as coming before the renewal settles (1(d)); and P11a's adoption looks
on every order that could hold a renewal's payment, `ordersHoldingCharge`, before any resubmission (1(e)).

  built here (Open question 20):

    absent or fails. Only the UI checks may fail open (Q-10); this server guard fails closed.
  - **The way out (P11a, P11b; D6b's P15 fills the port).** The renewal's stop port `erasurePending(ownerRef)` also

    resubmission for that owner, and P15's sweep ends the plan. The audit line is now `billing.renewal.owner_stopped`

**The shipped-corpus oracle.** Every task here that creates a shipped `.ts` file under `apps/` or `packages/` adds it
to `tests/support/shipped-corpus.manifest.txt` in its own commit (the D1/D5 convention;
`tests/unit/s1-1-depth-contract.test.ts` scans `packages`, `apps` and `web` and turns red on an unlisted file). The
step is the same in each task: run `SHIPPED_CORPUS_MANIFEST_UPDATE=1 pnpm exec vitest run
tests/unit/s1-1-depth-contract.test.ts`, then `git diff tests/support/shipped-corpus.manifest.txt` (only additions:
exactly the task's new paths, no removals), then the same test without the variable (PASS). The expected diff holds
only if every earlier fragment keeps the manifest in step as well (see Open questions). Coverage in this part
(checked for D6b's request): P7, P8a, P8b, P8c, P9a, P9b, P10a, P10b, P11a and P11b each create shipped files and
each carry the step, listing exactly the files they create (`codes`, `audit`, `records`, `single-flight`, `outbox`,
`email-job`, `runtime`, `packages/db/src/billing-jobs.ts`; `refusal`; `place`, `quote`; `rows`, `account-email`,
`checkout`, `charge-status`, `order-text`; `notice-intake`; `location-verdict`, `settlement`, `settlement-initial`,
`refunds`, `verify-payment`; `invoice-common`, `invoice-quaderno`; `invoice-smartbill`; `stored-tax-context`,
`renewal-rules`, `renewal`, `settlement-renewal`; `maintenance`, `renewal-notice-job`). P9c creates no file.

**The type check and the two source audits (D5's rule, D5 #2).** `pnpm run lint` is `pnpm run audit:architecture &&
pnpm run audit:source` (`package.json:17`), and at dev afbfe5ad (as at 24be86f5) `audit:architecture` already exits 1
on dev's three F31 edges (`tests/architecture/scaffold.test.ts:34-38`), so `lint` never reaches `audit:source`. No step here runs
`pnpm run lint`. Wherever a step says "the type check and the two audits", it runs these three, each on its OWN Run
line (never joined with `&&`, so a known-red audit cannot stop the next one):
- `pnpm run typecheck` — **Expected:** exit 0.
- `pnpm run audit:architecture` — **Expected:** exit 1, and `"violations"` is exactly dev's three lines
  `apps/api -> obs-capture is not a declared edge`, `apps/runner -> obs-capture is not a declared edge`,
  `apps/scheduler -> obs-capture is not a declared edge`, nothing else. An extra `apps/api -> <x> is not a declared
  edge` line for a package this part imports means the `apps/api` row of `tools/orphan-audit/src/index.ts` (the
  `["apps/api", "apps/api", [...]]` row, `:41` at afbfe5ad) and `apps/api/package.json` miss `<x>` (P7 Step 4 says how
  to add it).
- `pnpm run audit:source` — **Expected:** exit 1, and `"blocking"` is exactly dev's three lines (pinned at
  `tests/architecture/scaffold.test.ts:69-75`): `packages/obs-capture/install/api.ts reads the process environment
  outside the register loader`, the same for `runner.ts` and for `scheduler.ts`. Any other line fails the step (a new
  `process.env` read, a `switch` without `default:` + `exhaustive(`, a test import, a numeric export).

**Prices stay with the subscriber (Terms §12, spec §1.8 "Changing the price for existing subscribers").** Every
subscription carries its own recurring net price, written as `recurring_net_micros` next to
`announced_total_micros` on `ACTIVATED` (here, P9b), `UPGRADED` and `DOWNGRADE_SCHEDULED` (D6b's P12c/P12b). A
renewal (P11a) charges that net plus a freshly quoted tax, never `planById(plans).netPriceMicros`: a `billingPlans`
version published with a new price reaches only new checkouts, until the owner's price-change command (with its
30 days' notice) exists. P11a's `recurringNetOf(events)` is the one reader; D6b's upgrade proration uses the same
value as its old net (D6b already does).

**Build order inside this part:** P7 → P8a → P8b → P8c → P9a → P9b → P9c → P10a → P10b → P11a → P11b. Each task is
one reviewable commit. P8, P9, P10 and P11 were split into these lettered tasks because each was too large for one
reviewer.

#### New names (for the assembler)

Everything here is new; nothing in the contract was renamed. Names another task owns are consumed, not redefined:
B7a owns `installBillingRoutes`, `BillingRouteDeps`, `BillingRouteOptions`, `billingNotFound`, `BILLING_ROUTE_PATHS`,
`BillingRoutePath`, `BillingRoutePolicy`, `BillingUsageReader`, `PersonUsageReader`, main.ts's `billingRouteOptions`
and `PlanIdSchema` (R-3, R-4); L2 owns the consent manifest helpers; L4 owns the re-acceptance rule (`requiresReacceptance`); P1b owns
`LocationVerdict`; P4 owns `FakeTaxEngine`; P5 owns SmartBill's pacing.

**The R3 rebase (dev afbfe5ad).** P8a's `installBillingRoutes(...)` call in `apps/api/src/index.ts` hands the routes a
`source` (`BillingRequestSource`) that keeps only `ip` and `userAgent` from `sourceFor`, dropping the age gate's
optional `countryCode` (R3-3). For the age gate (R3-2, Open question 20) this part adds four names and renames one:
P8c's `BillingAgeConfirmation` and `BillingRouteDeps.ageConfirmation` (supplied only by `buildApi`, so
`BillingRouteOptions`'s `Omit` gains `"ageConfirmation"`), the refusal `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (403, new for the
contract's §9; `AGE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE`, 503, is the age gate's own code, reused), and the harness's `frozen` set; the
audit line `billing.renewal.erasure_pending` is renamed `billing.renewal.owner_stopped`. The migration numbers this
part cites are R3-1's (0081 entitlement, 0082 customers/subscriptions, 0083 charges/invoices, 0084 outbox/cancel).

    refundCreatedAt = null)`), `RefundIntent`,
    `PaidTransaction` (with `providerRefunded`), `RefundAllocation`, `paidTransactions`, `refundedMicros(charge,
    transactionId)` (one paid transaction's refunded amount, P1a's per-transaction count; P9c uses it), `allocateRefund`,
    `pendingRefund`, `refundedAlready` and `refundIntentOf`. A lookup that fails before a resend keeps the last call's
    not-sent stage as the retry code (`again`'s `retryCode`), so an outage longer than one retry never dead-letters a
    not-sent partial refund. Follow-ups: M11 (`CARD_COUNTRY_BLOCKED`),
    M11_DUPLICATE (`ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED`, `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED`, and `DUPLICATE_PAYMENT` per transaction), a credit

    is another one, and at the end of the not-final schedule for an unmatched rebill-looking success, D5 5f); the
    `refund` transaction dispatch (`paymentOf`, `refundTransaction`) and `duplicateStatus`; the unmatched rebill

    `recordDuplicatePayment(…, {amountMicros, reason})`; every read inside its transactions on the client.

**Elsewhere**

- **`packages/db/src/billing-jobs.ts` `BillingJobQueries`**, a sibling of P1b's repository for the SQL that is not a
  table write:
  - `lockOwner(client, ownerRef)`, with the A3 key `debateai.billing.owner:`.
  - `withLease(key, use)`: a session try-lock on any key, returning `RAN|BUSY`; `withSubscriptionLease(id, use)` is
    it on the key `debateai.billing.subscription:<id>`; RefundDesk uses `debateai.billing.refund-call:<txId>`.
  - `outboxJobExists(client, kind, ref)`. (The claim re-assert is P1b's `BillingRepository.renewClaim`; the earlier
    `BillingJobQueries.renewClaim` is gone.)
  - `chargeIdForTransaction(txId, kind|null, environment)` (P9b; one xMoney system, D5 5h), `markJobStage(jobId, code)`
    / `jobStage(jobId)` (P9b; P10b too), `smartBillDocument(series, number)` and
    `smartBillDocumentsNotAccepted(from, to)` (P10b; P16b's owner summary consumes the second),
    `openCharges({environment, kinds, after, closeBefore, renewalCloseBefore, limit})` (P11a; keyset on `(created_at,
    charge_id)`, leaving out charges with two or more SUBMIT_UNKNOWN until their close can be due: a renewal's own
    charge 72 hours after it was made, Q-1, a retry 24 hours after its latest unknown),
    `unverifiedRenewals({environment, periodStartFrom, periodStartTo, submittedBefore, after, limit})` (P11a, Q-1:
    attempt-1 RENEWAL charges SUBMITTED and not settled, same keyset) and `liveSubscriptionIds(after, limit)` (P11b).
  - `checkoutPaymentSignals(client, chargeId, environment, notFinalSince)` (P8c): a not-final notice, or a job last
    retried as PAYMENT_NOT_FINAL, counts only when newer than `notFinalSince`. `lockOwner` bounds its wait with
    `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '10s'`.

**Codes, events and keys**

- **Refusal codes:** `COUNTRY_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (409), `BILLING_ADDRESS_REQUIRED` (422, R-15),
  `CHECKOUT_PENDING` (409 with `charge_ref`, D7 #5) and `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (403, P8c, R3-2: the account
  still owes the age gate's one-time check) are new; the assembler adds `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (403) to the
  contract's §9. P8c's checkout also answers the age gate's own `AGE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` (503, already in
  `apps/api/src/index.ts:1884`) when the check cannot be read. The contract §9 codes are used as they are.
- **Admission scopes (contract §2, spec §2.7; R-9 / R-37),** added the way G3a adds `geo_availability`:
  - `billingQuote` (P8b): value member `billing_quote`, owner, 10 per hour, capacity 65 536 (quotes only).
  - `billingCheckout` (P8c): value member `billing_checkout`, owner, 10 per hour, capacity 65 536 (the checkout's own
    scope, spec §2.7; the number is proposed, V ratification pending).
  - `billingNotify` (P9a): value member `billing_notify`, source, 120 per minute, capacity 65 536, keyed by
    `clientIpNetworkScope(source.ip)` (an IPv6 caller's /64).
  - All three appear in `AdmissionPolicy`, in `AdmissionScope`, in `BillingAdmissionScope` and in
    `ADMISSION_POLICY_DEPLOYMENT_REGISTER_ROW` (the hosted register example carries no admission row today).
  - The boot refusal is `BILLING_ADMISSION_UNSEALED`.
- **Internal `TypedDomainError` codes:** `BILLING_ACCOUNT_EMAIL_UNAVAILABLE`, `BILLING_CUSTOMER_MISSING`,
  `BILLING_QUOTE_MISSING`, `BILLING_STORED_CONTEXT_MISSING`, `BILLING_SETTLEMENT_UNREGISTERED`,
  `BILLING_REVERSAL_UNHANDLED` (only between P9b and P9c), `BILLING_INVOICE_DATA_MISSING`, `REFUND_AMOUNT_INVALID`,
  `REFUND_EXCEEDS_CHARGE` from `allocateRefund` (the same code as P1b's trigger), `REFUND_TRANSACTION_ALREADY_REFUNDED`
  (`RefundDesk.requestAll`), `BILLING_RECURRING_PRICE_MISSING` (P11a: a history with no recorded net price),
  `EFACTURA_DOCUMENT_UNKNOWN` (P10b: the owner's reference names no SmartBill document) and
  `BILLING_LEASE_UNLOCK_FAILED`.
- **`billing.outbox.last_error_code` values:** `CHARGE_NOT_FOUND`, `PAYMENT_NOT_FINAL`, `OUTBOX_HANDLER_FAILED`,
  `EMAIL_PAYLOAD_INVALID`, `BILLING_PROFILE_MISSING`, `BILLING_PROFILE_UNREADABLE`, `EMAIL_ATTACHMENT_UNRESOLVED`,
  `REFUND_PAYLOAD_INVALID`, `REFUND_CHARGE_MISSING`, `REFUND_BUSY`, `REFUND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `REFUND_UNRECORDED`
  (a dead VERIFY_PAYMENT: a second refund made elsewhere on one payment, P9c),
  `REFUND_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE`, the stage `REFUND_CALL_STARTED`, `XMONEY_REFUSED`, `XMONEY_UNAVAILABLE` /
  `XMONEY_CREDENTIALS_REFUSED` (a refund call that sent nothing; retried, never killed), `INVOICE_CHARGE_NOT_PAID`,
  `INVOICE_ORIGINAL_MISSING`, `CREDIT_NOTE_PAYLOAD_INVALID`, `CREDIT_NOTE_MANUAL`, `INVOICE_UNKNOWN`,
  `TAX_SERVICE_REFUSED`, `INVOICE_SERVICE_REFUSED`, `INVOICE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, and the stage
  `INVOICE_CALL_STARTED`. The run report's `BILLING_OUTBOX_CLAIM_LOST` is never stored (the job belongs to the other
  process). P16's owner summary should list the dead `INVOICE_UNKNOWN`, `CREDIT_NOTE_MANUAL` and `XMONEY_REFUND`
  (`REFUND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `XMONEY_REFUSED`) jobs, the dead `SMARTBILL_INVOICE` / `SMARTBILL_STORNO` jobs whose code
  is `INVOICE_SERVICE_REFUSED` or `INVOICE_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (D5 5j: a missing Romanian legal invoice must always
  reach the owner), the stuck renewals, the dashboard refunds, the second refunds made elsewhere (the dead
  `VERIFY_PAYMENT` jobs whose code is `REFUND_UNRECORDED`, ref = the refund transaction; Open question 1), the
  subscriptions whose history does not fold (D6b's P16b lists all of these) and
  the SmartBill documents ANAF has not accepted (`smartBillDocumentsNotAccepted`, with D6b's `pnpm
  billing:efactura-status`).
- **`charge_event.error_code` values:** the failure codes above (with `NO_TRANSACTION` for a stuck renewal),
  `SUBMIT_UNKNOWN`'s `REBILL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` and `SUBMIT_INTERRUPTED`; on a later `REQUESTED` (a call marker or a
  call that sent nothing, D5 5i) `RESUBMIT_STARTED`, `REBILL_NOT_SENT` and `REBILL_CREDENTIALS_REFUSED`; the refund
  reasons on `REFUND_REQUESTED` / `REFUNDED`; `DUPLICATE_PAYMENT` on a chargeback of a second payment. The kind
  `DUPLICATE_PAYMENT` itself carries no code.
- **Audit events:** `billing.payment.mismatch`, `billing.payment.duplicate`, `billing.refund.refused`,
  `billing.refund.outcome_unknown`, `billing.refund.unrecorded`, `billing.outbox.dead`, `billing.renewal.unknown`
  (with `code`), `billing.renewal.stuck` (`attempt`, `code`), `billing.renewal.pending` (`code`, Q-1; the new code
  `PAYMENT_NOT_VERIFIED` for a sent renewal whose check has not settled it, and `TAX_SERVICE_REFUSED` for a refused
  quote), `billing.renewal.dunning_unpriced` (`attempt`, `code`), `billing.renewal.tax_refused` (`code`, `reason`),
  `billing.renewal.report` (`failed`, `taxRefused`), `billing.renewal.owner_stopped` (no field: the stop port named
  the owner, an erasure or an `age_frozen` account; it was `billing.renewal.erasure_pending`), `billing.renewal.history_invalid`
  (`count`, `code`), `billing.renewal.price_missing`, `billing.xmoney.credentials_refused` (`operation`: checkout,
  verify, rebill or refund), `billing.xmoney.row_rejected` (`operation`, `count`, `code`) and
  `billing.invoice.unknown`, beside the spec §2.7 list.
- **Subscription event `data` keys written here** (P2's fold reads them, R-23):
  - `CREATED {country_confirmed, ip_country, quote_id, xmoney_environment}` (D5 5h)
  - `ACTIVATED {charge_id, announced_total_micros, recurring_net_micros, reactivated}` (also from ENDED(ABANDONED),
    A8c; `recurring_net_micros` is Terms §12's price the subscriber keeps, which D6b's UPGRADED and
    DOWNGRADE_SCHEDULED also write)
  - `RENEWED | RECOVERED {charge_id, period_start, period_end}`
  - `DOWNGRADED {charge_id}`, written only on ACTIVE and immediately followed by `RENEWED` at the new plan
  - `PAST_DUE {charge_id, attempt, next_retry_at, first_failed_at}` (also PAST_DUE → PAST_DUE), or with `reason`
    (`TAX_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`) and no `charge_id` for an attempt the tax service could not price (Q-1); P2's fold
    reads neither key, so it takes both shapes unchanged
  - `ENDED {cause: CANCEL|DUNNING|ABANDONED|DISPUTE, reason?, charge_id?}` (DUNNING carries `charge_id` or, after an
    attempt with no charge, `reason`; CANCEL also from ACTIVE/PAST_DUE with no
    cancel pending, for a card from a blocked country; CANCEL from PAST_DUE with a cancel pending, P11b's sweep;
    ABANDONED reasons `NEW_CHECKOUT`, `CARD_COUNTRY_BLOCKED`, `ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED`, `SUPERSEDED`)
  - `SUSPENDED {charge_id}`
  - `RENEWAL_NOTICE_SENT {announced_total_micros, sent_at}` (on ACTIVE)
  - `RENEWAL_POSTPONED {until, reason: "NOTICE_PERIOD"}` (on ACTIVE)
  - read, not written, here: `CARD_CHANGED {charge_id, retry_now}` — P11b defines what `retry_now: true` means (a
    PAST_DUE retry due at once, R-34); D6b's P12e, later in the build order, is its writer, and P2's fold carries the
    key without reading it
- **Entitlement causes used:** B5's `RENEWAL_POSTPONED` and `PAST_DUE_GRACE` (R-22) and `RENEWAL_PENDING` (Q-1),
  which extend `paid_through` (A8a); every append passes `monthCreditOverrideMicros: null`.
- **`billing.invoice_status_event` values written here** (P1a's CHECK `^[A-Z_]{1,32}$`): `SENT_BY_ACCOUNT_SETTING`
  (P10b, with every SmartBill document), `ACCEPTED` and `REJECTED` (the owner's, through `recordEfacturaStatus`).
- **`charge_event.xmoney_created_at` (D5 5m)** is written on SUCCEEDED and DUPLICATE_PAYMENT (P9b) and on a REFUNDED
  that sits on its own refund transaction (P9b's RefundDesk, P9c); never on a status change of the payment itself.
- **`billing.quote` rows written here:** kind `SUBSCRIBE` (P8b) and `RENEWAL` (P11a's renewal and every dunning
  retry, each priced afresh), each with `recurringTotalMicros: null`.
- **Job refs:**
  - `VERIFY_PAYMENT`: the xMoney transaction id, with payload `{notice_id, order_id, external_order_id}` or
    `{charge_id}`.
  - `XMONEY_REFUND`: `${chargeId}:${transactionId}`, with payload `{charge_id, transaction_id, amount_micros, whole,
    owner_ref, reason}`.
  - Invoice jobs: the charge id, with payload `{card_country, ip_country}`.
  - Credit notes: `${chargeId}:${transactionId}`, with payload `{charge_id, transaction_id, refund_micros}`.
  - `RENEWAL_NOTICE`: `${subscriptionId}:${periodEndIso}`.
  - `EMAIL`: `${template}:${dedupeRef}`. The dedupe refs are: M1 sub, M2 charge, M3 `sub:periodEnd:total`,
    M4 `sub:year`, M5A–C charge (or `sub:periodStart:attempt` for an attempt with no charge, Q-1), M6 sub, M7 `sub:accessEndIso`, M8 sub (queued by RefundDesk's WITHDRAWAL follow-up,
    which D6b's P12d adds because it reads P12d's `WITHDRAWN.data.refund_micros`), M10 charge, M11 charge,
    M11_DUPLICATE charge (`ALREADY_SUBSCRIBED`, `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED`) or `charge:transaction` (a `DUPLICATE_PAYMENT`,
    one per refunded transaction), O2 `charge:transaction` (Q-5: a refund that could not be completed, one per refund
    job).
  - M1's params: `withdrawalDays` only in a withdrawal country; its `ACCEPTED_TERMS` fields `{version, sha256,
    locale}` from L3a's widened `latest(ownerRef, "TERMS")` (empty when none is on record, which the billing gate
    makes unreachable in production).
  - O2's params: `chargeRef` (our 32-hex charge id), `refundAmount` (decimal, "12.10"), `reasonCode` (the dead-letter
    code: `XMONEY_REFUSED`, `REFUND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`, `REFUND_CHARGE_MISSING`, `REFUND_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE` or an
    unknown call outcome once its schedule is spent); recipient OWNER, locale English.

**Decisions to confirm with the owner or the accountant**

7. **A tax REFUSAL at renewal (the outage past 72 hours is settled by Q-1).** Q-1's outage past 72 hours is built as
   the ruling says: the normal dunning starts with no charge row (PAST_DUE, its grace, M5A), and every retry is priced
   afresh, so no period is ever charged from the old end after days on Free. What Q-1 does not name is
   `TAX_SERVICE_REFUSED` (a revoked Quaderno key, a 422): permanent until someone fixes it, so this part treats it as
   an operator alarm (`billing.renewal.tax_refused`, once per subscription period per process, and the tick's
   `billing.renewal.report`), never dunning and never a charge. For paid access it follows the plan's precedent for
   xMoney's refused key: the same 72-hour `RENEWAL_PENDING` hold, labelled `TAX_SERVICE_REFUSED`; past it access
   lapses at `paid_through` while the renewal keeps quoting each tick. The owner should pick one of three readings:
   (a) that hold (built), (b) stop at once (no hold, access ends at the period end), or (c) an owner-listed hold that
   lasts until the owner fixes the key (a longer `RENEWAL_PENDING`, needing a ruling on how long). D6b's P16b lists
   the blocked subscriptions either way (it builds that list).
8. **Q-1's other edges.** (a) A not-sent rebill is sent again, within the 72 hours, with the amount its own quote gave
   when the charge row was written (a new amount would need a second attempt-1 row, which A2's unique key forbids).
   (b) A2 stays binding inside the window: after an unknown outcome the rebill is submitted once more at most; the
   rest of the "quiet retries" is adoption. (c) Q-1 covers the renewal itself: a dunning retry (attempts 2–4) whose
   calls never reach xMoney stays REQUESTED on its backoff with no close (its `PAST_DUE_GRACE` already ends access
   on time), so an xMoney outage that outlasts the whole dunning leaves the subscription PAST_DUE until xMoney answers.
   (d) The window counts from a notice postponement's end when A7 postponed the renewal past the period end.
9. **Refused-card payments.** A payment refused for a blocked card country, and refunded at once, gets no invoice and
   no credit note. The same holds for a duplicate payment on an order already paid (P9b, `DUPLICATE_PAYMENT`; D5's
   `quarterSummaryRows` never counts its refund as a REFUND row). Confirm with the accountant.
10. **One credit note per charge.** 0083 makes invoices unique per `(charge_id, kind)`, so a second refund on the same
    charge goes dead as `CREDIT_NOTE_MANUAL` for the owner.
11. **Dashboard refund amount.** A refund made in the xMoney dashboard that xMoney reports as its own `refund`
    transaction is recorded at that transaction's amount, with its credit note (P9c, D5's model). One reported only as
    the payment turning `refund-ok` is recorded for what is left of that one paid transaction (a duplicate payment's
    own refund on the same charge never counts against it), an upper bound (item 5). Its
    effects: no automatic credit note (a `billing.invoice.unknown` `CREDIT_NOTE_MANUAL` line, and P16b's list); the
    transaction is marked `providerRefunded`, so a later withdrawal over it goes to the owner rather than silently
    refunding 0.00. A void or cancel after success is a refund in full (A9) and gets its credit note at once.
12. **Checkout reuse (A3b), tightened.** A young CREATED checkout is reused only for the same plan, total and xMoney
    system, and only while its charge has no outcome; otherwise it is abandoned and a new charge is made. While a
    payment for it is on its way (a notice, an open check, an xMoney transaction that is not `complete-failed`) it is
    neither reused nor abandoned: 409 `CHECKOUT_PENDING` (D7 #5), a not-final attempt only while it is fresh (item 4d).
    A used quote answers `QUOTE_EXPIRED`. A payment for
    the reused order made twice is still refunded (P9b's duplicate path). The in-flight listing matches on
    `externalOrderId`, which P3b reads only when xMoney returns it on a transaction (X0): the notice and the open job
    are the checks that hold without it.
13. **The checkout's admission number.** The checkout has its own scope `billingCheckout` (spec §2.7); its number
    (owner, 10 an hour, like the quote) is proposed and needs the owner's ratification (V-1).
14. **Retry schedules** live inside functions (the failure schedule; A9's not-final schedule; the not-sent rebill
    backoff; Q-1's 72 hours as `renewalPendingMs()` and the unverified pass's `unverifiedLookBackMs`; the 3-D Secure
    attempt's life as `inFlightAttemptLifeMs()`; the owner lock's 10-second `lock_timeout`). Move them to
    `billingPolicy` if they must be tunable.
15. **Invoice details.** The invoice line is worded in the buyer's locale through the `orderText` port (English until
    P17/P18's catalogue sentences, which D7 builds), with the dates in that locale; the INITIAL charge's line carries
    the month that began at the activation, not the checkout's provisional period. SmartBill invoices are Romanian
    documents: with the catalogue sentences a Romanian buyer's line is Romanian; confirm that a non-Romanian buyer
    taxed in Romania (rare) may get a line in their own language. The e-Factura answer is not read from SmartBill (no
    API read, X1 row 10): the owner records it with D6b's `pnpm billing:efactura-status`.
16. **The renewal passes** fold every live subscription in TypeScript (paged over `subscription_latest_v`), as P1b's
    `dueRenewals` does; fine at launch scale. A tick pages at most 20 × 50 due subscriptions, 20 × 50 open charges and
    20 × 50 unverified renewals; the rest wait one tick (60 s).
17. **Q-1 and a sent renewal whose check never settles.** A rebill that answered (SUBMITTED) is "an outcome still
    unknown" while VERIFY_PAYMENT cannot settle it (3-D Secure pending, xMoney unreadable), so the plan is held
    (`RENEWAL_PENDING`, code `PAYMENT_NOT_VERIFIED`) for up to 72 hours past the due instant. Q-1 then says dunning
    starts; this part does NOT close such a charge `FAILED(NO_TRANSACTION)`, because a real transaction exists and may
    have moved money: the hold lapses at its `paid_through` (A8a), and VERIFY_PAYMENT (until its job dies) and P14a's
    daily reconciler still own the outcome; a late success renews the plan, a late decline takes the normal failure
    path. The owner should confirm that a charged person may drop to Free after 72 hours while the payment itself is
    still unknown, rather than being dunned for money they may already have paid.
18. **A dunning retry is priced afresh, without an A7 notice.** Q-1's "no charge without a fresh quote" makes every
    retry quote the tax again at the subscriber's own net (a retry used to copy the first attempt's amount). If the tax
    rate moved during the days of dunning, a retry charges the new total without M3's 7-business-day notice (the net
    never moves; a tax change is the only difference). The owner should confirm this, or rule that such a retry sends
    M3 and waits.
19. **The API pool waits for a connection for ever.** With every billing read under the owner lock on its own
    transaction (P8c's rule and test) and the lock bounded to 10 seconds, the known starvation is closed. `main.ts`
    still builds the pool with `createPool(DATABASE_URL)` and pg's default `connectionTimeoutMillis: 0`, so an
    unrelated starvation would still queue for ever; `createPool`'s options admit only `max` today. Giving the main pool
    a finite `connectionTimeoutMillis` (a `packages/db` change, every pool at once) is left to the owner.
20. **A paid plan and the age gate (R3-2): now built; two questions stay with the owner.** The risk: an account
    created before the date-of-birth field owes a one-time age check; answered under 18, 0077's
    `identity.confirm_account_age_with_audit` revokes every session and sets `age_frozen`, and a plan bought before
    that would be billed every month for a service the person can no longer sign in to, with no way left to stop it.
    What this part now builds:
    - **The way in is closed (P8c).** `POST /v1/billing/checkout` asks the age gate's own reader
      (`SessionApplication.readAgeConfirmation`, the one `GET /v1/auth/age-confirmation` answers from, so no grant
      is added) before L4's legal gate: while the check is owed it refuses 403 `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` and never
      starts a checkout; when the reader is absent or fails it refuses 503 `AGE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE`. This server guard
      fails closed; only the UI checks (`AuthGate`, P19's `/checkout` redirect) may fail open (Q-10). Because a passed
      record is final, an account past this guard is never frozen by the age gate afterwards.
    - **The way out, for any `age_frozen` owner all the same (P11a, P11b, with D6b's P15).** The renewal's stop port
      (`erasurePending`, asked by `erasureBlocks` before every rebill, dunning retry, retry charge and adoption
      resubmission) answers true for an `age_frozen` owner once P15 widens `billing.owner_erasure_pending` and
      `billing.pending_erasure_owner_refs` in its own 0086 (not yet applied, so it is widened, not superseded: D6b's
      option (a)). P15's sweep then calls `stop(ownerRef)`: `ERASURE_STOPPED` (ENDED) and a FREE entitlement.
      Skipping alone would not do, because P11b's period-end sweep never ends an ACTIVE plan a renewal keeps
      skipping. The audit line is `billing.renewal.owner_stopped`, content-free, never read as an erasure. Only
      `age_frozen` is tested, not "not active" (`suspended` is the erasure's PREPARED state, 0040:5596, already
      covered; `pending_mfa` is before activation).
    Still the owner's (with counsel for the first): (a) whether money already taken from a person who then told the
    service they are under 18 is refunded (the contract with a minor): nothing here refunds it, and no billing default
    decides it; and (b) whether P13's cancel link should also reach an `age_frozen` account (today it goes only to a
    `state='active'` one, D6b), so the person or a parent can stop the plan by email in the time before P15's sweep
    ends it (the sweep runs every 10 minutes).
21. **Seller facts outside `COMPANY` (R3-4).** Nothing here writes a seller fact. SmartBill's company code is not a
    setting: there is no `SMARTBILL_COMPANY_CIF` (D5 dropped it). P6a builds the issuer's `companyCif` with
    `smartBillCompanyCif(SELLER_COMPANY)` (the CUI in the bare form, `vat.number` in the RO form, as
    `SMARTBILL_CIF_FORM` in `apps/api/src/billing/connectors.ts` chooses, X1 row 16) and refuses to switch billing on
    while the fact it needs is still bracketed (`BILLING_COMPANY_FACTS_UNVERIFIED:cui`, and `:vat` in the RO form).
    The test that the mirror equals `COMPANY` is P6a's `tests/unit/billing-seller-company.test.tsx`; nothing is asked
    of P17 for it. This part reads the same mirror for its one seller word: P8c's `order-text.ts` takes the brand of

### Notes from part D6b

These tasks sit on P1–P11. They add everything a subscriber does after checkout (upgrade, downgrade, cancel, withdraw,
change card, read invoices), the cancel-without-signing-in route, the daily money check against xMoney, the owner's
dispute and withdrawal commands, the erasure hook, and the owner's tax summary. AMENDMENTS-R1 overrides the spec; the items used here are A1, A2, A3, A4, A6, A7,
A8, A9, A10, A12, A15, A17, A18, A21, A22, A25 and A26. The reconciliation rulings applied here are R-3, R-4, R-7,
R-8, R-17, R-18, R-29 … R-39, and the owner's rulings R2 Q-1 (a renewal outage keeps the plan: P12b's cancel and
M7), Q-4 (M7 links to Settings), Q-5 (RefundDesk emails O2 for a dead refund: nothing here to build), Q-6 (the
withdrawal window is 14 calendar days, no weekend or holiday roll: P12b), Q-7 (no downgrade quote), Q-9 (the owner's
withdrawal command runs P12d's withdrawal: P14c), Q-13 (`billingCancelLink` by source network: P13), Q-14 as
renumbered by R3-1 (0085 and 0086 appended in build order: P12a, P15) and Q-15 (the shipped-corpus manifest check in
every task: P12a checks it is unchanged, every other task regenerates it). D6a's requests of this part are built as well: every billing file here
keeps P8c's transaction-read rule (its architecture test runs in each Step 4 that touches `apps/api/src/billing`);
P16b lists the renewals Q-1 leaves without a charge (a dunning the tax service could not price, and a renewal a tax
refusal blocks) and the second refunds made elsewhere that P9c could not record (`REFUND_UNRECORDED`); P16b builds the
owner's e-Factura command `pnpm billing:efactura-status` on P10b's pieces; P15 ends the live plan of an account the
age gate froze (R3-2) and never records that stop as an erasure; and P14a's adoption looks on every order P11a's
`ordersHoldingCharge` names, the check P11a's own adoption makes. The
tax summary and its O1 email count only the live xMoney system's payments (D5's `quarterSummaryRows` takes the
system; a sandbox payment is never a sale).

**The rebase onto dev afbfe5ad (RULINGS-R3, binding over everything above and below).** The base is now origin/dev
afbfe5ad: the colleague's age gate (PR #41: `migrations/0077_age_gate.sql`, the account state `age_frozen`, the date
of birth on sign-up), the legal pages and footer (PR #42: `/legal`, `/terms`, `/terms/versions`, `/privacy`,
`/cookies`, `/providers`, the `COMPANY` constant) and the i18n and dependency fixes (#37, #38, #39); the colleague's
open branch `feat/sensitive-data-consent` reserves `0078`. What that changes in this part:
- **R3-1, the migration numbers.** This part's migrations are `migrations/0085_billing_withdrawal_step_up.sql` (P12a)
  and `migrations/0086_billing_erasure_hook.sql` (P15). The ones they build on are L3a's `0079_legal_acceptance.sql`,
  B5's `0081_billing_entitlement.sql` and P1a's `0082_billing_customers_subscriptions.sql`,
  `0083_billing_charges_invoices.sql` and `0084_billing_outbox_cancel.sql`; the scorecard is `0087`. Every number in
  this part was mapped by R3-1's old → new table (0077 → 0079 … 0085 → 0087), prose, SQL identifiers and error codes
  alike. At afbfe5ad the pinned list of `tests/architecture/security-migration-0065.test.ts` ends with
  `"0077_age_gate.sql"` (line 424); it gains `"0078_sensitive_data_consent.sql"` when the colleague's branch merges,
  then L3a's, B3's, B5's and P1a's entries, and P12a and P15 append theirs after P1a's `0084_billing_outbox_cancel.sql`.
  Before creating its migration, each of the two tasks runs `ls migrations | tail -3` (R3-1's executor rule, its Step
  0).
- **R3-2, account states.** `identity."user".state` now also takes `age_frozen` (next to `pending_verification`,
  `pending_mfa`, `active`, `suspended`, `deleted`): a refused one-time age check revokes every session of the account
  and freezes it. Every account read in this part that must find a live person tests `state='active'` — P12a's
  `billing.consume_withdrawal_grant`, P13's cancel-link lookup, and P15's route hook through
  `identity.schedule_account_erasure`'s own active-account lock (`identity.lock_account_t9_internal(p_user_id, true)`)
  — and so stays correct: a frozen account holds no session, cannot step up or schedule an erasure, and is sent no
  cancel link. A frozen account's live paid plan is ended instead (D6a's request, open question 18): P15's
  `billing.owner_erasure_pending` also answers true for an owner whose account is `age_frozen`, so P11a's stop port
  (`erasureBlocks`, its content-free line `billing.renewal.owner_stopped`) refuses every rebill, dunning retry and
  resubmission, and `billing.pending_erasure_owner_refs` lists such an owner, so P15's 10-minute sweep writes
  `ERASURE_STOPPED` (marked `data.stopped_for: "AGE_FROZEN"`, audit `billing.age_frozen.stopped`, never read as an
  erasure) and the FREE entitlement; P8c's checkout guard (`AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`) keeps an account that still owes
  its check from buying. The one state list this part enumerates is P15's, and it names only `age_frozen`, never "not
  active" (`suspended` is the erasure's PREPARED state, `migrations/0040_account_erasure.sql:5596`, which the erasure
  lists already cover; `pending_mfa` comes before activation). No test here posts `POST /v1/billing/checkout` through
  `buildApi` (the money path goes through the harness's `checkoutWith` / `buy`), so P8c's age guard needs no
  `readAgeConfirmation` in this part's session stand-ins.
- **R3-3, the country source.** Nothing here reads a country from a request header: the age gate's `edgeCountry`
  (`cf-ipcountry`, `apps/api/src/index.ts:1496`) is G3a's to reconcile with its `CountryGate`, and the one country
  decision this part makes — the place of an upgrade's or a card check's payment — goes through P8b's
  `decidePaymentPlace({geo, policy, ip, declaredCountry})` and G2's `decideCardCountry`, unchanged.
- **R3-4, company facts.** Nothing in this part needs the seller's name, address, CUI, VAT code, phone or email: the

withdrawal command) and P16 into three (P16a register row, P16b summary command, P16c owner jobs). Build order inside

  starts. So an ACTIVE subscription can be read here with its period end already behind it: P12b's cancel then ends
  the plan at once, in its own transaction (ENDED(CANCEL) and FREE effective now; M7 dated today, `canUndo:
  "false"`), exactly as it does once a RENEWAL charge for the next period exists, because a renewal already in flight
  can no longer be stopped by the cancel flag alone; and P12c's upgrade is refused inside and past the renewal's

  (`renewalLeadMs`), P12c (a renewal waits for an unsettled upgrade of its period, holding the plan with Q-1's
  `holdPending`, code `UPGRADE_UNSETTLED`), P12e (`rebillOutcomeOpen`, the recovery's own "may this rebill have
  reached xMoney" rule, exported for the card change).

  dead-letter path, P9b/P17, not this part's).

  `apps/api/src/billing/index.ts`). G3a (and ruling Q-13) make it the rule: every SOURCE-keyed admission scope is

**The checks every Step 4 runs** (D6a's part intro, D5's rule). `pnpm run lint` is `pnpm run audit:architecture &&
pnpm run audit:source` (`package.json:17`), and at dev afbfe5ad `audit:architecture` already exits 1 on dev's three
F31 edges, so `lint` never reaches `audit:source`: no step here runs `lint`. (The three lines of each audit were
measured at 24be86f5. The colleague's merge up to afbfe5ad changed no `package.json`, nothing under
`tools/orphan-audit/`, added no `process.env` read outside `apps/ui`, and its new kernel constants — `MIN_AGE = 18 as
const`, `AGE_REFUSAL_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60` — do not match the numeric-export pattern of
`tools/orphan-audit/src/index.ts:697`, so the expected lines stand. Both audits need `pnpm run generate:contract`'s
output to start, which a read-only check could not write: the executor's first Step 4 confirms the lines, and a
fourth line that no task of this part caused is reported, not fixed here.) Each step runs, every command on its OWN
Run line (a known-red audit never stops the next one):
- `pnpm run typecheck` (after `pnpm run generate:contract` where the task changes the contract) — exit 0;
- `pnpm run audit:architecture` — exit 1, and `"violations"` is exactly dev's three lines `apps/api -> obs-capture is
  not a declared edge`, `apps/runner -> obs-capture is not a declared edge`, `apps/scheduler -> obs-capture is not a
  declared edge`, nothing else;
- `pnpm run audit:source` — exit 1, and `"blocking"` is exactly dev's three lines `packages/obs-capture/install/api.ts
  reads the process environment outside the register loader` and the same for `runner.ts` and `scheduler.ts`,
  nothing else (a new `process.env` read, a `switch` without `default:` + `exhaustive(`, a test import or a numeric
  export would add one);
- in every task that adds or edits a file under `apps/api/src/billing` (all but P12a and P16a), P8c's
  `pnpm exec vitest run tests/architecture/billing-transaction-reads.test.ts` — PASS (D6a's 4a). The test scans
  every file under `apps/api/src/billing` as an AST: inside a `withTransaction` callback, a function with a
  parameter named `client`, or one that takes `client` out of a settlement context, each `subscriptionForOwner`,
  `subscriptionsForOwner`, `subscriptionEvents`, `chargesForSubscription`, `charge`, `quote`, `customerByOwner` or
  `latestProfile` read on a `…repository` / `…billing` receiver passes that client, and `acceptances.latest`,
  `entitlements.current`, `erasureBlocks`, `erasurePending` and `freshQuote` are not called there at all. Every
  billing source this part writes (the new files and the edits to D6a's) was run through that scanner while writing
  this revision: no offence (the reads that do not pass a client are all in tests, which the rule does not scan).

#### New names (for the assembler)

**Numbers and citations (RULINGS-R3).** This revision renumbers by R3-1 (P12a's migration 0083 → 0085, P15's 0084 →
0086; the tables it builds on 0079 → 0081 and 0080–0082 → 0082–0084; L3a's legal migration 0077 → 0079), including
the SQL identifiers and verify codes that carried the numbers, and re-measures every file:line against dev afbfe5ad
(R3-7). For R3 itself it adds two Step 0 checks (`ls migrations | tail -3`), one P12a integration test (an
`age_frozen` account's grant is refused) and one P13 assertion (an `age_frozen` account gets no link).

**This round (the cross-requests after R3).** Built from D6a's requests: P15's two erasure lists also name an
`age_frozen` account (R3-2's state list for the erasure sweep; widened in 0086 itself, which no host has applied), a
third lookup `billing.owner_age_frozen` / `BillingRepository.ownerAgeFrozen`, the mark `ERASURE_STOPPED.data.stopped_for:
"AGE_FROZEN"` and the audit line `billing.age_frozen.stopped` (so a frozen account's stop is never read as an
erasure), one P15 integration case and P15's unit test on P11a's renamed `billing.renewal.owner_stopped`; P8a's
`Omit` as P8c widens it (`| "ageConfirmation"`); P16b's `REFUND_UNRECORDED` payment check over P9c's dead
`VERIFY_PAYMENT` jobs (`BillingRepository.unrecordedRefunds(since)`, one integration case; P16c's Pick and fake gain
it); and P14a's `adoptOne` looking on every order P11a's `ordersHoldingCharge` names (one integration case), with the
P12e / P14a prose now saying P11a looks on every order that could hold the payment (P12e's guard stays, as defense in
depth).

**Task split.** P12 → P12a (step-up purpose, migration 0085), P12b (reads, cancel, revoke, downgrade + the module),
P12c (upgrade + UPGRADE settlement), P12d (withdraw through RefundDesk), P12e (card change + CARD_CHECK settlement).
P14 → P14a (reconciler), P14b (dispute command), P14c (withdrawal command, D7 #36 and R2 Q-9: Q-9 names P12d as
the owner of `pnpm billing:withdraw --owner <ref>`; the command is P12d's `recordWithdrawal` run by the owner, and it
stays its own task after P14b because it needs P14b's operator connection, which P12d cannot consume under the build
order). P16 → P16a (register row), P16b
(summary + command, and the e-Factura status command D6a asked for), P16c (owner job and the retention purge). Nothing below redefines a name another task owns; the consumed names are listed in the
preamble and each task. Where a task edits an earlier task's file (P7's `audit.ts`, P8a's `refusal.ts`, P8b's
`quote.ts`, P8c's `checkout.ts`, P9b's `refunds.ts` / `settlement-initial.ts`, P11a's `renewal-rules.ts` /
`renewal.ts`, `packages/db/src/index.ts`'s `createPool`), the edit sits in the task whose test needs it and is listed
in its Files; the edits that use a name made later (P15's `ownerErasurePending` in P8b/P8c/P9b's files, P12d's
`WITHDRAWN.data.refund_micros` in RefundDesk) cannot move earlier.

**Every task that creates a shipped file** (under `apps/` or `packages/`) regenerates
`tests/support/shipped-corpus.manifest.txt` in its own Step 4 (`SHIPPED_CORPUS_MANIFEST_UPDATE=1 …`, the diff adds
exactly that task's paths), reruns the test without the variable and commits it: P12b, P12c, P12d, P12e, P13, P14a,
P14b, P14c, P15, P16a, P16b, P16c (P12a creates only a migration and tests, so it runs the corpus test and
`git diff --exit-code` on the manifest instead: R2 Q-15). No commit
stages `packages/contract/generated` (it is git-ignored; `pnpm run generate:contract` is a local check).

**Every Step 4 runs the type check and the two audits on separate Run lines, never `pnpm run lint`** (the preamble's
"checks every Step 4 runs": at dev afbfe5ad, as at 24be86f5, `audit:architecture` already exits 1 on dev's three `obs-capture` edges,
so `lint` would stop there), and every task that adds or edits a file under `apps/api/src/billing` (P12b–P12e, P13,
P14a–P14c, P15, P16b, P16c) also runs P8c's `tests/architecture/billing-transaction-reads.test.ts` (D6a's 4a).

**Every read under the owner lock uses the transaction's connection** (P12b's rule), through P1b's trailing
`executor` parameter (asked of D5) and the `executor` of every method this part adds: `lockedSubscription`,
`requestCancelLocked`, `prepareUpgrade`, `recordWithdrawal`, `startCardChange`, the CARD_CHECK and UPGRADE
settlements, `cancelByToken`, `CancelLinkService.request`, `failWithoutTransaction`, the dispute command, the
withdrawal command's settlement (`withdrawalsAwaitingOwner`) and RefundDesk's WITHDRAWAL follow-up. A lease holder
never asks the pool for a second connection either: the upgrade runs its transactions on the lease's own
(`withTransactionOn`). Pool-of-one (pool-of-two under an operator pool) regression tests: `cancelForOwner`,
`cancelByToken`, `withdraw`, `startUpgrade` (and three upgrades at once on a pool of three), the dispute command, the
withdrawal command.

2. **Where Q-9's command lives.** R2 Q-9 names P12d as the owner of `pnpm billing:withdraw --owner <ref>`. The

   `loadBillingOperatorEnvironment` from P14b into P12d (then P14b and P14c consume them from P12d).
3. **Refund reason for an upgrade that can no longer apply** (the subscription went PAST_DUE, a renewal closed its
   period, an erasure began, or it is already on the plan). The upgrade settlement answers `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED`, so
   M11_DUPLICATE's wording ("you already have an active plan") goes out; the same holds for a first payment refunded
   during an erasure or after an age-gate freeze (P15). The owner may want its own sentence, which would need a new
   reason in P7 and P9b.
4. **The card-check hold's statuses** are assumed: `auth` mode reports `complete-ok` when authorized, and `void-ok`
   or `refund-ok` after the release. Whether `auth` accepts 0.00 is also open (A12). X0 confirms both;
   `cardCheckHoldMicros` (`card-change.ts`) is the one place to change.
5. **Owner decisions still open.** An erasure hook that fails still answers 202 (the settlements' refund and the
   10-minute sweep close the gap); the tax texts are the research of 29 September 2026, for the accountant.
6. **An upgrade whose rebill never left (P12c, D5 5i).** A 429, a refused connection or a refused key leaves the
   UPGRADE charge `REQUESTED` and answers 503; P14a's adoption pass settles it `FAILED(NO_TRANSACTION)` about 30–40
   minutes later. Until then a new upgrade answers `UPGRADE_IN_PROGRESS` (the charge could be one whose process died
   mid-call, so it cannot be told apart safely). If the owner prefers an immediate retry, the not-sent case needs
   its own charge-event kind (P1a's CHECK), an owner ruling on A2.
7. **Second refunds made outside our code, until X0 is green** (D5 5n). A listed `refund`-type transaction counts as
   settled when a REFUNDED exists under its own id or on a payment it names, so a second partial refund of a payment
   we already refunded once is not queued for VERIFY_PAYMENT by P14a. When a notice brings one, P9c hands it to the
   owner with its durable mark (a dead `VERIFY_PAYMENT` job with `REFUND_UNRECORDED`), which P16b now lists as
   `REFUND_UNRECORDED`; one that no notice reports is not seen until then. Once X0's refund recordings are green, P14a
   can read P3b's `refundsOf` rows that no REFUNDED of ours names, as D5 5n describes for P9c (such a row would then
   reach P9c and the same list); not built before that.
8. **Finding the owner ref for an emailed withdrawal (P14c).** The command takes `--owner <ref>` (R2 Q-9). A person
   who writes from their account's address can be found only through the email blind index, whose key the operator
   environment does not load; today the owner reads the ref from the person's support case (`identity_owner_ref`).
   A `--email` lookup would need the blind-index key in `loadBillingOperatorEnvironment` (a custody decision).
9. **Stuck renewals and unrecorded refunds in the owner summary** (`RENEWAL_STUCK`, `REFUND_UNRECORDED`) are listed
   for 120 days after they were closed or first dead (A10's charge-back and refund windows): the rows carry no
   "checked" marker. If the owner wants them listed until resolved, the resolution needs its own record (for an
   unrecorded refund, for example a command that records its amount against the charge, which P1a's
   one-request-per-transaction key would have to admit).
10. **The upgrade's recorded net comes from this process's register.** `UPGRADED.recurring_net_micros` is the new
    plan's price in the register the API booted with (the quote row has no field for it, and P1a's migration is not
    this part's). A restart onto a new `billingPlans` version between an upgrade's quote and its payment (minutes)
    would record the new price while the announced total is the quoted one; P11a's fresh quote then differs from the
    announced total and A7 sends M3 before any different charge. A `quote.recurring_net_micros` column (P1a) would
    remove the gap; not asked, since the notice already protects the subscriber.
11. **A cancel inside the renewal's 5-minute lead ends the paid access up to `renewalLeadMs()` early (P12b).** Once a
    RENEWAL charge for the next period exists, the cancel cannot stop the renewal by its flag, so it ends the plan at
    once and the renewal's money goes back. Keeping those minutes would need D6a to refund an ACTIVE plan's renewal
    when a cancel is pending (the settlement refunds only PAST_DUE ones today) AND the revoke route to refuse while a
    RENEWAL charge for the period exists — without the second, cancel, refund, undo would leave an ACTIVE plan that
    `createCharge` never renews. Not built; the owner may prefer it.
12. **An erasure owner whose history does not fold (P15).** The sweep now runs isolated from the money check, but that
    owner fails every stop, so `[BILLING_ERASURE_SWEEP_PENDING]` repeats every 10 minutes until the developer repairs
    the history (P16b lists the subscription as `SUBSCRIPTION_HISTORY_INVALID`). Optional hardening, not built: catch
    `BILLING_SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS_INVALID` per owner in `sweep`, count it in one content-free audit line (e.g.
    `billing.erasure.history_invalid {count}`) and not rethrow, so the pending line means only new failures.
13. **The owner's dashboard figure is trusted (P14c).** `--dashboard` is what the owner says was refunded in the xMoney
    dashboard for the withdrawal; it is bounded only by what the withdrawal's payments took
    (`BILLING_WITHDRAW_EXCEEDS_PAID`), since xMoney's read names no refunded amount (X0 may show a better source).
14. **The tax summary counts the live xMoney system only (P16b, P16c).** D5's `quarterSummaryRows` now takes the
    system; `liveQuarterSummaryRows` always asks `"live"` (D7's runbook already says "the quarterly tax summary and
    its email read only live charges", and a sandbox payment is never a sale). *Assumed:* that holds on every host,
    so a host still on xMoney's sandbox prints and emails a summary with no sales. The owner may prefer a
    `--environment stage` flag on the command for a rehearsal; it would be one argument of the CLI's reader, never of
    O1.
15. **Each quarter's e-Factura list holds the documents issued in that quarter (P16b, P10b's query).** P10b's
    `smartBillDocumentsNotAccepted(from, to)` selects by the document's issue time, so a document ANAF has not
    accepted is listed in its own quarter's summary (and every rerun of `pnpm billing:tax-summary` for that quarter)
    but not in later ones. *Assumed:* the quarterly reminder is enough, since the owner records the answer within
    days. If the owner wants every open document in every summary, P16b would ask P10b's read with `from` at the
    first SmartBill document instead of the quarter's start, and the section heading would say so.
16. **How a blocked renewal is found (P16b's `blockedRenewals`).** The durable trace of a tax refusal is P11a's lapsed
    `RENEWAL_PENDING` (the refusal code itself is only the content-free `billing.renewal.tax_refused` line, R-25), so
    the list reads "the entitlement in force is a lapsed RENEWAL_PENDING of an ACTIVE subscription, and no RENEWAL
    charge exists for its period". Any other hold that outlives its 72 hours with nothing written would be listed the
    same way, which is also worth the owner's look. It stays listed until a charge is written for the period or the
    subscription changes state, with no age limit: a renewal that cannot be priced is not settled by time passing.
17. **Where P14c's settlement table lives (R2 Q-14 as renumbered by R3-1).** R3-1 fixes the billing migrations at
    0081–0086 (P12a owns 0085, P15 owns 0086, the scorecard 0087), so P14c cannot add one.
    `billing.withdrawal_owner_settlement` is created in P12a's `migrations/0085_billing_withdrawal_step_up.sql`, the
    one withdrawal migration built before P14c, keyed to its WITHDRAWN event with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so D5's
    `billing.purge_expired_records` (0084) removes it unchanged (its returned count does not include the cascaded
    rows). The assembler accepts 0085 as its home or amends R3-1.
18. **An age-frozen account with a live paid plan (R3-2): now built; two questions stay with the owner.** The risk:
    the age gate's one-time check for an existing account (0077's `identity.confirm_account_age_with_audit`) revokes
    every session and sets `age_frozen` when the person answers under 18, while every way to stop a plan bought before
    is closed to them (Settings needs a session, P12d's withdrawal needs a step-up grant —
    `billing.consume_withdrawal_grant` tests `state='active'` —, a frozen account cannot schedule an erasure, and P13
    sends a cancel link only to an `active` account, pinned by P13's test). What is built (D6a's request, the earlier
    option (a)):
    - **The way in (D6a's P8c).** `POST /v1/billing/checkout` refuses 403 `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` while the account
      still owes its check, and 503 `AGE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` when the age gate's reader is absent or fails (fail
      closed). A passed record is final, so an account past this guard is never frozen afterwards; only accounts that
      bought before the guard existed can be.
    - **The way out (D6a's P11a/P11b, with P15 here).** P15's 0086 widens `billing.owner_erasure_pending` and
      `billing.pending_erasure_owner_refs` to an `age_frozen` owner (0086 is not applied anywhere yet, so it is widened
      in place, not superseded). P11a's stop port then refuses every rebill, dunning retry, retry charge and
      resubmission (`billing.renewal.owner_stopped`), and P15's 10-minute sweep writes `ERASURE_STOPPED` and the FREE
      entitlement. The stop is told apart from an erasure where it is recorded (P2's fold has one stop kind, so both
      read ENDED with cause ERASURE): `billing.owner_age_frozen`, read under the owner lock, marks the row
      `data.stopped_for: "AGE_FROZEN"`, and the audit line is `billing.age_frozen.stopped`. The owner summary (P16b)
      lists no stops at all, so nothing there reads a frozen account's stop as an erasure; the sweep's failure line
      `[BILLING_ERASURE_SWEEP_PENDING]` is the one stop sweep's, for both. Only `age_frozen` is named, never "not
      active", and P15's integration case pins it against a real account (a `pending_mfa` owner is the control).
    Still the owner's, with counsel for the first: (a) whether money already taken from a person who then told the
    service they are under 18 is refunded (the contract with a minor). Nothing here refunds it and no billing default
    decides it; the plans concerned are the `ERASURE_STOPPED` rows with `data ->> 'stopped_for' = 'AGE_FROZEN'`, and
    a refund would go through P9b's `RefundDesk` (a ruling would say which payments and how far back). (b) Whether
    P13's cancel link should also reach an `age_frozen` account (today it goes only to a `state='active'` one), so the
    person or a parent can stop the plan by email in the minutes before the sweep ends it; with the sweep in place the
    link would only ever find the plan already ended or about to be.
19. **The reserved 0078 and the order migrations run in (R3-1).** If our 0079–0086 are applied on a database before
    the colleague's `0078_sensitive_data_consent.sql` merges, `migrate()` (`packages/db/src/index.ts:823-852`: it
    sorts the file names, skips each one already in `public.debateai_schema_migration` and applies the rest) applies
    0078 later, after them. *Assumed harmless:* 0078 creates only
    `identity.sensitive_data_consent` and its two functions, which no migration of ours reads or writes, and ours
    touch nothing it creates; the pinned list in `security-migration-0065.test.ts` is kept in file-name order either
    way (0078 goes between `0077_age_gate.sql` and L3a's `0079_legal_acceptance.sql`). No host outside development
    has applied any of ours yet.
20. **The stop sweep reads the account table by state (P15, R3-2).** `billing.pending_erasure_owner_refs` now also
    selects `identity."user"` rows with `state='age_frozen'`; no index covers `state` (the table's indexes are its
    unique columns, 0031's `audit_token` and 0037's `owner_ref`), so each 10-minute sweep scans the account table
    once. *Assumed
    acceptable* at the expected number of accounts (the erasure part already reads `legal.account_closure` whole each
    tick); a partial index `ON identity."user"(owner_ref) WHERE state='age_frozen'` would be an identity-schema change
    for a later migration if the table grows, never an edit of 0086 once it is applied anywhere.
21. **Refunds made after a freeze use the erasure's wording (P15, open questions 3 and 18).** A payment that lands
    after the freeze is refunded as `SUBSCRIPTION_ENDED` (M11's "you already have an active plan" wording, as during an
    erasure), sent to the account's billing address although the person can no longer sign in. The owner may prefer
    no email, or a sentence of its own, for an `age_frozen` owner; either needs a new refund reason (P7, P9b) and is
    left with open question 18's ruling.

### Notes from part D7

These seven tasks come last in Part 2, and an eighth closes it. They sit on top of P1–P16: the billing tables, the
connectors, the API routes and the jobs. They add four things:

- **the email templates**: 35 locales, and one sending path;
- **every billing page**: pricing, checkout, the card form, Settings, cancel and withdraw, and the paid-plan
  additions to the colleague's legal pages and site footer (PR #42 built those; R3-4);
- **the operations**: the runbook, a pin on the example register rows, the go-live rows, and the whole-flow test;
- **the Part 2 pull request** (P24): merge the latest `origin/dev`, run every Part 2 integration suite by hand (CI
  skips them), open the PR to `dev`, fix what CI and review find, and merge when green, billing still off.

Eight rules hold in every task:

- **RULINGS-R3 is binding and wins over everything below.** The design branch now contains `origin/dev` afbfe5ad
  (merged as d4b6cd8f): the colleague's age gate (PR #41, `migrations/0077_age_gate.sql`), the legal pages and the
  site footer (PR #42, with the one `COMPANY` constant in `apps/ui/lib/legal/pages.ts:70-88`), and the i18n and
  dependency fixes (#37, #38, #39). Every file:line, function name and test pin below is re-measured against that
  tree (R3-7). The R3 rulings these tasks apply are R3-1 (P24's migration numbers: ours are `0079`–`0087`, `0078` is
  the colleague's reserved consent migration), R3-2 (P19's checkout sends an account that still owes its one-time age
  check to the age gate's interstitial first, and so does its flow on P8c's server refusal; P23's accounts carry the
  age record registration writes, and its session application reads it), R3-3 (P23's age records get the country the
  country gate would record, never decisive), R3-4 (P17's emails read `COMPANY` through P6a's one mirror
  `SELLER_COMPANY`, never a `_merchant.json` or a copy of their own; P21 copies its `COMPANY.vat` change into that
  mirror; P22 tells the owner the CUI is digits only and names no CIF setting; P21 EXTENDS the colleague's `/legal`
  and footer and creates only `/cancel`, `/withdraw`, `/privacy/versions` and the one-text pages; `/terms/versions`
  is L2's to feed), R3-5 (P19
  carries `next=/checkout?plan=…` with the age gate's constant-prefix return path only, no second carrier) and R3-6
  (P24 merges the colleague's consent branch the way its files need).
- **RULINGS-R2 and AMENDMENTS-R1 override the spec, and RECONCILE-DECISIONS overrides the contract.** The rulings of
  29 September these tasks depend on are Q-1 (P22 tells the owner a renewal outage keeps the plan for up to 3 days,
  and P20's Settings card promises no date already past meanwhile), Q-2 (the notice address's `200`/`429`/`500`,
  P22), Q-3 (P17 attaches the ACCEPTED Terms from L2's archive `apps/ui/legal/archive/<locale>/<sha256>.md`, and P21
  serves the `/privacy/versions` list the Privacy Policy promises and one page per archived text of both documents,
  beside the colleague's `/terms/versions`), Q-4 (M7 links to Settings), Q-5 (the owner template `O2` for a
  refund that could not be completed), Q-6 (the withdrawal window is 14 calendar days), Q-7 (the downgrade confirm
  names the lower plan's net price from `GET /v1/billing/plans`, "+ tax, from {date}"), Q-8 (the `/new` chooser is
  B10a's), Q-9 (a withdrawal sent by email is carried out with D6b's `pnpm billing:withdraw`, P21 and P22), Q-12 (the
  records key is the sixth escrowed secret, P22's row 21), Q-15 (the shipped-corpus step) and Q-16 (P17's package
  rows). The amendments are A2 (P23's adapter keeps the adoption check in real time), A7 (the upgrade shows the price
  it announces), A11 (the card-form policy), A12 (the card change), A14 (the DB-IP credit stays with billing off),
  A22 (`sdk_environment`), A25 (the cancel links) and A26 (the package rows and the mail format). The reconciliation
  rulings are R-3 (`BillingRouteDeps` is B7a's, extended by P8a), R-7 (`PUBLIC_APP_URL`, never
  `PUBLIC_SITE_ORIGIN`), R-8 with Q-5 (these seventeen mail ids are final), R-15 (Romanian buyers give name, city and
  county), R-16 (fakes live in `acceptance/billing-fakes/`, tests import them through `tests/support/`), R-26 (P23's
  fake stack stands in for a laptop hosted profile) and R-27 (P18 regenerates the legal manifest).
- **These tasks are last in the build order** (after P16; P24 after P23). They create no API route and no
  migration. Every name they take from P1–P16, B1–B11 and L1–G4 is consumed exactly as that task defines it; see each
  task's Interfaces.
- **The source audits run on their own lines.** `pnpm run lint` is `audit:architecture && audit:source`, and at dev
  afbfe5ad (as at 24be86f5) `audit:architecture` already exits 1 on dev's three F31 edges, so `lint` never reaches `audit:source`. No
  step here runs `pnpm run lint`: each runs `pnpm run audit:architecture` and `pnpm run audit:source` separately, and
  each is expected to exit 1 with exactly dev's three baseline lines (D5's part intro lists them) and nothing else.
- **English is authoritative.** The other 34 catalogues are produced the way PR #21 did it: an AI translator seat
  works offline, every `{placeholder}` must survive, and then the parity checks run.
- **The UI stays free of hard-coded English.** Every visible string comes from a catalogue, and the English
  scanner's allow-list stays empty.
- **Every new shipped file goes into the shipped-corpus oracle.** Each task regenerates
  `tests/support/shipped-corpus.manifest.txt` in its own commit step.
- **Every new page is a support-catalogue entry, and V signs the catalogue.** `tests/architecture/support-catalog-coverage.test.ts:26-54`
  (run by `test:ci-gate`, not in `tests/ci-known-red.txt`) finds every `apps/ui/app/**/page.tsx` and requires
  `SUPPORT_PAGE_ROUTES` (built from `SUPPORT_CAPABILITIES`, `packages/support-kb/src/catalog.ts:193-427`) to name
  exactly those routes. The catalogue's bytes carry V's signature: `packages/support-kb/reviews/manifest.json:3-11`
  holds `catalog.sha256` (`reviewedBy: "OWNER"`), `packages/support-kb/src/index.ts:656` admits reviewed articles only
  while it matches, and the API's boot-time corpus load (`apps/api/src/main.ts:109-115`, `requireReviewedRecovery:
  true`) refuses otherwise, so an unsigned catalogue stops the API. P18–P21 create nine pages (`/pricing`;
  `/checkout`, `/checkout/return`; `/settings/card`; `/cancel`, `/withdraw`, `/privacy/versions`,
  `/terms/versions/[sha256]`, `/privacy/versions/[sha256]`). P18's Step 0 (OWNER-RUN) collects V's signature once,
  for the four states the catalogue passes through, and each page task adds its own entries and applies its own
  signed fingerprint in its own commit, with the pins that move with it. No entry has an action (no `pricing` action
  either: `support-catalog-coverage.test.ts:128` stays), no article text changes, and no agent signs.

The 35 locales, in `apps/ui/lib/i18n/locales.ts` order:
`bg hr cs da nl en et fi fr de el hu ga it lv lt mt pl pt ro ru sk sl es sv uk zh hi id ja ko vi ar he tr`.

#### Open questions (for the assembler)

1. **O2 (ruling Q-5) is settled on both sides.** P17 renders `O2`; D6a's P7 already carries `"O2"` in
   `BillingMailTemplateId` and `TEMPLATE_IDS` (P17's `SAME_IDS` pin compiles against it), and D6a's
   `RefundDesk.deadLetter` enqueues it with ``dedupeRef: `${intent.chargeId}:${intent.transactionId}` `` (the refund
   job's own ref) and `params: {chargeRef: intent.chargeId, refundAmount: microsToDecimal(intent.amountMicros),
   reasonCode: code}`. Left for the assembler: the contract's §4 `MailTemplateId` and R-8's list gain `O2`.
2. **The Terms archive is read through the manifest, as D1 asks (ruling Q-3), settled.** P17's `ACCEPTED_TERMS`
   resolver first asks L2's `archivedDocument("TERMS", locale, sha256)` (the manifest's sha256 → path map; null →
   `MAIL_TERMS_NOT_ARCHIVED`), then reads `apps/ui/legal/archive/<locale>/<sha256>.md` through `termsArchivePath`
   (the file L2's `legalArchivePath` names and the entry's `path` points at, pinned by a test) and verifies the bytes
   against the name. The low-level `acceptedTermsAttachment` stays manifest-free, so its tests still run on a
   temporary legal root, and a new case proves that a sound file the manifest does not list is never attached. One
   difference from D1's wording: a hash the manifest never archived logs `MAIL_TERMS_NOT_ARCHIVED`, not
   `MAIL_TERMS_NOT_RECORDED`, because the acceptance row exists and names a text that was never published;
   `MAIL_TERMS_NOT_RECORDED` stays for no row or malformed fields. P17's repository test (`finds the repository's own
   archived Terms …`) fails until L2 has archived the current English Terms, so the gap cannot pass unseen.
3. **Which archived texts the previous-versions pages list (owner or counsel), and who owns which page (R3-4).**
   PR #42 built `/terms/versions` over a hand-kept `TERMS_VERSIONS` (`apps/ui/lib/legal/pages.ts:152`); R3-4 gives L2
   the choice of feeding it from the archive. P21 no longer touches that list: it builds `/privacy/versions` (the
   Privacy Policy promises it and nobody else built it) and one page per archived text of both documents over L2's
   `legalArchive` / `archivedDocument`, inside the colleague's `LegalPageLayout`. L2's archive also keeps the
   pre-go-live draft texts that were never in force (D1's Open question 9). *Assumed:* `/privacy/versions` shows
   everything archived, newest first, the one in force tagged "Current". The owner or counsel may prefer only the
   versions published from go-live on; that is a filter in `LegalArchiveVersionsBody` alone (and whatever L2 chose
   for `/terms/versions`), and the one-text pages keep answering for any archived hash, since M1 attaches the
   accepted version from the same archive. If the assembler would rather L2 also served `/privacy/versions` and the
   one-text pages, P21's three pages, `LegalArchiveBodies.tsx` and `archive.ts` move to L2 as written.
4. **The xMoney SDK's option names** (`paymentForm` options, `onPaymentComplete`, `submit()`/`destroy()`,
   `displaySubmitButton`, `displaySaveCardOption`) are not confirmed by the OpenAPI copy. They live in
   `apps/ui/lib/billing/xmoneySdk.ts` alone, and X0's sandbox recording must confirm them. `form-action` and COOP are
   also X0 measurements: P19 includes `form-action`, and P22 documents the Caddy pop-up matcher as conditional.
5. **Where the paid-plan parts of the footer show (R3-4).** The colleague's footer is site-wide: the one-line shape on
   every page, the full shape on the landing and the legal pages. P21 extends only the full shape (through an optional
   prop) and gives the pages that take money (`/pricing`, `/checkout`, `/checkout/return`, `/cancel`, `/withdraw`) the
   full shape too. The one-line shape stays as it is, because knowing whether billing is on would cost every page,
   the debate canvas included, one plans read against the visitor's public-read admission. So the DB-IP credit, the
   card marks and the billing links are on the landing, every legal page and every billing page, but not in the
   one-line footer of the other screens (the sign-up page included, whose country gate uses DB-IP). *Assumed:* that
   satisfies xMoney's rules (the shop and legal pages) and DB-IP's CC BY 4.0 credit ("on the site"). If counsel wants
   the credit on every page, it is one fixed link in the line shape (the colleague's line-footer case at
   `legal-pages.test.tsx:351-369` then pins one more `href`), and it needs no billing state.
6. **The return path after email verification (R3-5, settled).** No browser storage carries `next` any more: the age
   gate's constant-prefix `safeReturnPath` is the one mechanism, now accepting `/checkout`, `/checkout/return` and
   `/settings/card`. It carries `next` from `/login?next=…` through both sign-in steps and the age interstitial, and
   the sign-up page's "Log in" link keeps it. The mailed verification link carries no `next`, so a person who finishes
   in the email's tab lands on the default page and reaches the plan again from `/pricing`; one who returns to the
   sign-up tab and presses "Log in" goes straight to the checkout. If the owner wants the email's tab to return to the
   plan as well, the carrier would be a `next` inside the mailed link (an API change to the registration mail), not a
   second UI mechanism.
7. **The address on `/withdraw` (ruling Q-9).** Terms §13 says "write to [support@dezbatere.ro]", while `COMPANY`
   (`apps/ui/lib/legal/pages.ts:80-86`, R3-4) has `emails.general` "[hello@dezbatere.ro]" and no support address.

   both with the same inbox; a separate support inbox would need a sixth `COMPANY.emails` member (the colleague's
   constant, with its tests) or a Terms edit.
8. **P23 composes the runtime with every required dep.** The stack passes P8a's `legal` gate as a stub, for the

   one TERMS row, which L4 in hosted mode (`owedWithoutRecord`) would send to the accept screen, and L4's own suites
   own that rule. It passes `buildApi({billing: {...runtime.routes, usage}})`:
   `BillingRuntime.routes` is P8a's `BillingRouteOptions`, B7a's `usage` member included (R-3). It reads

   executor (R-32: `RefundDesk` as the `XMONEY_REFUND` handler), P12a's widened step-up route, and that the runtime
   builds P9b's acceptance read from `deps.pool` itself, so the stack passes nothing new.

    charges stay in the database, but they never count as sales: the quarterly tax summary and its email read only
    live charges" holds as written when P16b and P16c pass `"live"` to D5's `quarterSummaryRows(from, to,

    charges); the sentence would then need "once the host points at live". D6b still calls it with two arguments
