    reuses the checkout's `billing.checkout.reacceptRequired`, which does not say where to accept: Settings and the
    card page show no accept screen (D1: `/settings` passes `legalGate={false}` to `AuthGate`, and `/settings/card`
    uses no `AuthGate`), while `/new` and `/debate` do. If the owner wants the sentence to link there, it becomes a
    sentence with a link to `/new` in P20 (one more key). `CARD_CHANGE_NOT_AVAILABLE_NOW`
    and `FAILED(CARD_CHECK_DEFERRED)` share `billing.card.tryAgainShortly` (see item 13 for its wording).
29. **The emails' company facts: P6a's one mirror, `SELLER_COMPANY` (R3-4, P17's decision; D5's R3-B, applied).**
    R3-4 let P17 choose how the mail reads `COMPANY`, with one source of truth, and asks for "a single mirrored source
    for the API/mail package". P6a (earlier in the build order) already built that mirror, `SELLER_COMPANY` in
    `@debateai/billing-core`, pinned `toEqual(COMPANY)` by `tests/unit/billing-seller-company.test.tsx`. So P17 reads it
    and keeps no copy of its own: the previous revision's generated `messages/_company.json` and its
    `COMPANY_FACTS_UPDATE=1` generator would have been a second mirror. The price is one declared edge,
    `mail-templates -> billing-core` (billing-core depends on `kernel` alone, so no cycle), and one rule for the owner:
    after an edit of `COMPANY`, copy the same values into `packages/billing-core/src/company.ts` in the same commit
    (P22 §14.7 says so, and two tests fail otherwise). P21's `COMPANY.vat` change does exactly that. For the assembler:
    the plan now has one company mirror (`SELLER_COMPANY`), read by P6a, P8c (the brand word), P17 and P22's
    runbook; nothing reads a `_company.json`.
30. **`COMPANY.vat` is changed by P21 (R3-4).** R3-4 records the owner's confirmation that DebateAIRO S.R.L. is
    VAT-registered, so P21 sets `vat: {kind: "registered", number: "[RO…]"}` in the colleague's constant, copies the
    same value into P6a's `SELLER_COMPANY.vat` in the same commit (D5's request: its mirror test is
    `toEqual(COMPANY)`), and moves the one pin of the colleague's suite that named the old sentence
    (`tests/render/legal-pages.test.tsx:185`); the notice then shows "[RO…]" until the owner fills the code. While
    SmartBill takes the bare CUI, the bracketed number blocks nothing; in SmartBill's RO form P6a refuses it at boot
    (`BILLING_COMPANY_FACTS_UNVERIFIED:vat`). If the colleague prefers to make the `COMPANY` change himself, P21 drops
    the two `vat` lines (both files) and its `/legal` VAT case, and everything else stands. Still open for the owner
    (D5's R3-C, not this fragment's to decide): whether billing should refuse to switch on while any seller fact
    (office, register number, phone, emails) is bracketed; today P22's go-live row 18 is that check, by hand.
31. **Pins of the colleague's suites that P21 moves on purpose (R3-4, extended not recreated).**
    `apps/ui/lib/i18n/legal.test.mjs:84` (13 -> 20 footer and navigation labels: the seven `chrome.footer.*` keys) and
    its `ownedFiles` (P21's five legal files); `tests/render/legal-pages.test.tsx:185` (the VAT row, item 30) and
    `:389` (the landing's `<SiteFooter variant="full" billing={footerBilling} />`). Every other case of both suites runs
    unchanged, the line footer's exact link list included.
32. **The checkout asks the age gate first (R3-2), and the server has the last word (D6a's P8c).** `/checkout` uses no
    `AuthGate`, so an account created before the date-of-birth field, signed in from before the age gate, could
    otherwise reach the card form without its one-time age check. P19's checkout page asks `ageConfirmationOwed` and
    redirects to the age gate's interstitial with the plan as `next` (the age gate's own `ageConfirmationHref`). That
    read fails open, so D6a's P8c now guards the checkout route itself (403 `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`, 503
    `AGE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE`, failing closed), and P19's `CheckoutFlow` sends a 403 to the same interstitial and words
    a 503 "Something went wrong. Please try again." (D6a's Open question 6b, applied). `/checkout/return` and
    `/settings/card` do not ask: the first only reads a charge already paid, and every subscriber reached the card page
    through a checkout that asked. The card change's own route (P12e) has no age guard; if the owner wants one there
    too, it is P8c's `refuseUnconfirmedAge` in D6b's card-change route and one more branch in P20's `CardChangeFlow`.
    For the assembler: contract §9 gains `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` (403), D6a's request.
33. **No `/contact` page and no footer "Contact" link (R3-4, spec §2.16).** Spec §2.10 named a `/contact` page and a
    footer "Contact" link; spec §2.16 and R3-4 replace both with the colleague's legal notice, whose section 02 ("How
    to reach us") gives the phone and every email from `COMPANY` (xMoney's requirement). The footer's "Legal notice"
    link reaches it. If xMoney's reviewer asks for a link named "Contact", it is one more `PRODUCT_LINKS` row to
    `/legal#legal-section-02` and one chrome key.
34. **The consent branch meets Part 2 at P24's merge (R3-6).** `feat/sensitive-data-consent` rewords the Terms and the
    Privacy Policy in all 35 locales (the consent moves from sign-up to before the first debate) and adds `0078`. Once
    it is on `dev`, P24's merge runs `pnpm run generate:legal`, so L2's archive holds the new texts before the
    `generate:legal:check` gate, and orders the pinned migration list `0077`, `0078`, then `0079`+. Whether the
    rewording needs a new Terms version number, a re-acceptance floor (L4) or both is the colleague's and the owners'
    call, not this program's.
35. **The support catalogue for the nine paid-plan pages (P18 Step 0, OWNER-RUN).** Every page must be a
    support-catalogue entry (`tests/architecture/support-catalog-coverage.test.ts`), and the catalogue is V's signature
    (the API does not start on an unsigned one). P18 Step 0 asks V three things before any P18 change, and the
    build waits for V's answers: (a) whether the help assistant may name `/cancel` (variant A, public with no action,
    recommended: the page only asks for an email and sends a one-time link, whose key rides in the fragment, and
    cancelling needs a POST) or never (variant B, `excluded` like `/verify-email`); (b) four fingerprints, one per page
    task (recommended; every commit stays green) or one for the final catalogue (the fallback: P18–P20 keep exactly one
    red test, the route coverage, and P21 makes the whole catalogue change; nothing is pushed before P24 either way);
    (c) whether `app-navigation` ("Pricing is an informational section, not a checkout") and `budget-tier-choice` ("does
    not prove a paid subscription, checkout …") are reworded now or before billing is switched on. The plan assumes
    "before go-live": both sentences are true while billing is off, and a rewording changes the two article pairs, the
    recovery texts bound to them (`packages/support-kb/recovery/components.json`) and their review records, which is a
    support-content change of its own with its own signature. For the assembler: the go-live checklist (P22's rows
    14–26) has no row for it yet; one line in row 24 ("the legal texts match what billing does") or a new row 27 would
    carry it, with P22's pinned test moved accordingly.
36. **The entries' words are chosen to leave the reviewed support answers unchanged.** The support suites pin the
    answers to the 26 public question cases (`tests/support-eval/cases`), among them SUP-B-01 ("How much does the
    product cost, and which paid plan should I buy?", expected: no source). So no entry shares two scoring words with
    it (for example `billing-pricing` says "Plans and prices", never "paid plan"), and none uses "public", "debate" or
    "private", which the answerable cases rely on. Step 0 proves each of the four states on the real suites before V
    signs. Once billing is on, SUP-B-01's expectation (paid plans do not exist) is no longer true; changing it is part
    of the same go-live support change as (c) above, not of Part 2.
37. **A client-sent `cf-ipcountry` at the hosted edge (D1's Open question 8): measured, no Caddy change.** D1 asked P22
    to strip the header in the hosted Caddyfile if Caddy can reach the API without the UI. It cannot:
    `deploy/vps/Caddyfile:49` proxies every request to the UI (`127.0.0.1:3001`), the API listens on loopback only
    (`:4-5`), and the UI's `/api` proxy forwards only its `REQUEST_HEADER_ALLOWLIST`, which has no `cf-ipcountry`
    (`apps/ui/app/api/[...path]/route.ts:14-31`). So a forged header never reaches the age gate's `edgeCountry` from
    outside, and P22 leaves the Caddyfile (pinned by `tests/architecture/vps-deployment-baseline.test.ts`) untouched.
    A local process on the box could still post to `127.0.0.1:8790` directly; that is the existing loopback trust, and
    the recorded country is never decisive. If the owner wants a belt anyway, it is one `request_header -Cf-Ipcountry`
    line inside the `reverse_proxy` block and one pin in that test.
38. **The checkout's age refusals in the UI and the harness (D6a's Open question 6b), applied.** P19's `CheckoutFlow`
    sends P8c's 403 `AGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` to the age gate's interstitial (`ageConfirmationHref("/checkout?plan=…")`)
    and words the 503 `AGE_CHECK_UNAVAILABLE` with `billing.checkout.genericError`; P23's stack adds
    `readAgeConfirmation` over 0077's `identity.read_age_check_outcome` and a sixth whole-flow case for the 403. No
    other test in this fragment posts the checkout through `buildApi`: P19's and P20's are render tests with a mocked
    client. Any other fragment's test that does, with its own session application, needs the reader too (D6a's note:
    dev's `testSessionApplication` has none).

  `serve_reserve_attempts: serveSites * input.organMaxAttempts`; the age gate's edits sit outside all six):
  1. `packages/register/src/index.ts` `computeStructuralCeilingBasis` auto-merges to
     `serve_reserve_attempts: serveSites * input.organMaxAttempts`, but under DR-184-v5 `per_site_attempts.organ`
     is `serveSiteAttempts` (main + backup) and dev's parser (`packages/budget/src/index.ts`
     `costEnvelopeBasisSchema` superRefine) requires `reserve === call_sites.serve × per_site_attempts.organ`:
     **every v5 receipt would be refused at the run head** (`RUN_COST_ENVELOPE_UNRESOLVED`).
  2. `apps/runner/src/index.ts` `callSynthesisRole` auto-merges into a body that uses dev's `request`
     parameter inside the scorecard's `(call, site, organFailureCode)` signature (a typecheck failure).
  3. The scorecard's `buildSynthesisRolePrompt(request)` (the one builder the runner and `moment:replay` share,
     A17) builds **without** dev's argument-language directive (`promptContractInArgumentLanguage`, D2); the
     seat-caller closures for judge/review/panel calls omit `argumentLanguageName`. A merged run would silently
     lose the question-language rule on every scorecard-assigned call, and replayed moments would no longer be
     the live prompt.
  4. `migrations/0076_serve_disclosure.sql` refuses a served ref ≠ planned ref unless `fallback_reason = 'MONEY'`
     (`serve_disclosure_writer_fallback_is_coherent`, `…_fallback_names_its_reason`). On an assigned run the
     writer/checker come from the pinned seats, and a backup switch is not a money fallback: with dev's planned
     refs (the sealed role refs, `apps/runner/src/index.ts` `buildServeDisclosureRecord` call at `:6331-6339`) every
     assigned answer whose seat is not the sealed ref would be written as a false MONEY fallback. Two more traps sit
     in the same closures: dev's served refs are `served.servedBy.providerRef` (`:5982-5987`, `:6074`), which is the
     PLANNED maker object whenever no money fallback ran (`callServeRoleWithFallback` returns
     `servedBy: input.planned`, `:2172`), never the seat member that actually answered; and an assigned run must
     never resolve the sealed ref at all — the scorecard's claim leaves an assigned seat's sealed ref out of
     `synthesisMakers` (`sealedRefRoles`, scorecard runner `:3306-3311`; `synthesisMakers` is the debaters, `:3294`),
     so `resolveSynthesisRoleMaker` (`:5512-5529`) throws `SYNTHESIS_ROLE_PROVIDER_UNRESOLVED` for any writer or
     checker seat outside the debaters, after the whole debate was argued and paid for.
  5. `submit`'s run-setup steps (dev PR #33, `RunSetupStep`) do not cover the scorecard's pin insert, so a failed
     pin would leave a run showing "generating" forever — and B6b's `#submitWithRoom` (the hosted path with a room)
     does not pin at all, so on the website every scorecard-admitted run would lose its assignment.
  6. **Predicted from B9's plan text (not yet in any tree):** B9b exempts the first position's own call from the
     shared wall by `request.callSiteKey === FIRST_POSITION_CALL_SITE_KEY` (`"JUDGE"`), and B9c names a moved first
     call `RUN_FIRST_CALL` by the same comparison, looks a review's author up by the bare key and records who served
     each call by the request's key. On an assigned run every seat call carries `:seat:main` / `:seat:runnerUp`
     (`seatCallSiteKey`, scorecard `packages/serve/src/synthesis.ts:356`), so the first position would be walled (a
     started debate could get no first position), a moved first call would be misnamed, and a review could move onto
     its node's actual author. And an assigned seat's judge is built over the RAW configured provider
     (`buildAssignedRunSeatBook` `memberOf`, scorecard `apps/runner/src/run-seats.ts:276-280`), so B9c's cheaper
     model while arguing would never apply on an assigned run.

1. **S1a 7k is derived from B9's plan text, not from a merged tree.** The seat-marker comparisons, the moved B9c
   block and `judgeGatewayFor` follow D4's B9b/B9c code as planned; the merge's typecheck and B9's own suites are the
   oracle. The same holds for B9c's panel rule carried through 7a (`:4977`, `panelDegradationOf`) and 7f
   (`runJudgePanel`, `PanelMemberFailure`): it is D4's B9c text word for word, and B9c's pin and panel cases plus
   `judgement-s04` are its oracle in Step 9. If `ServeRoleMaker` needs more than `ConfiguredSeatMaker`'s four members, `bodyGatewayFor`'s parameter
   takes the runner's configured-maker type instead (owner: D4 / the S1a implementer).
2. **"Answer part vs serveMicros".** Implemented as "the whole run ≤ serveMicros" because both ceilings measure the
   run's one total (`attemptCeilingForPhase`); a literal "answer part ≤ serveMicros" would let a run exceed the
   serve ceiling. Owner to confirm.
3. **A null estimate at site scope only** keeps today's behaviour (assigned, `ESTIMATE_UNAVAILABLE`), because a
   strict "never fits" would refuse every hosted debate with a FALLBACK seat. Against a person's room it is the run
   maximum, as the spec says. Owner to confirm.
4. **Serve disclosure (0076) on assigned runs.** S1a records the member each round's seat asked first as planned,
   and the member that answered as served; a backup switch overwrites planned with the member that answered, so
   0076's MONEY-only fallback CHECKs stay true and the switch is disclosed by BACKUP-MODEL-USED and the ledger's
   switch records. An owner who wants backups in `serve.serve_disclosure` itself needs a new migration (the next
   free prefix after the scorecard's 0087) adding a reason such as `'BACKUP'`; not planned.
5. **The argument language in moments** (S1a 7m (d)) was not on the scorecard's own merge checklist; it adds an
   optional member to the moment's builder `inputs` (the private evaluator treats `inputs` as opaque per the
   scorecard's A18 rulings, and a default-language moment's id is unchanged) — confirm with the evaluator's contract
   before the owners' first pilot run.
6. **S1b English.** 0 owner picks were recorded on 29 September; if picks exist when S1b runs, the controller
   substitutes them in English before translation (the handover page, collection `picks`).
7. **The evaluator's default caps.** debateai-evaluator's `src/config.ts:141` defaults `planStrengthCaps` to
   `{ "free": "BALANCED" }`, which S2 refuses with billing on. Changing that default is an evaluator-repository
   change this plan cannot make; the owners are told in S1a's OWNER-RUN item 6 and both READMEs.
8. **The boot check with a scorecard in force (B9d's hand-off, taken in S2).** With a VALID scorecard the picker may
   seat any discovered target for any plan (`reachableInTodaysOrder`: roster first, then every other healthy
   target), so S2 prices every configured, priced model for every plan: the check then asks that the cheapest
   configured model's first call fits, which is looser than the roster rule when a cheap model sits on no roster,
   and stricter when no roster is wholly configured (the roster rule then checks nothing). Assumed: this is the
   rule B9d's "every plan's cheapest must fit" means on the picker path, because no plan has a model subset of its
   own there (plan caps limit the STRENGTH, not the models). If a later scorecard version gives plans their own
   model lists, `firstCallPlanModels` is the one place that must follow it (owner: D4 / the scorecard's owners).
   The runner asks the same sealed `modelScorecard` row as the hosted API at its own `REGISTER_VERSION`; both units
   are pinned to one version (runbook §11), so they agree.
9. **A dev migration that takes the scorecard's number before the Part 3 PR merges.** RULINGS-R3 R3-1 fixes the
   scorecard at 0087 and gives the rule for a later collision: S1a Step 1 and S3 Step 1 run `ls migrations | tail -3`
   and, when dev has taken 0087 (or sorts a file after it), shift the scorecard's file alone to the next free prefix
   in one commit that says so — it is the only one of ours not yet on dev, and it is idempotent, so a development
   database that applied it as 0072 or 0087 re-applies it harmlessly under the new name. Assumed: R3-1's "shift ALL
   of ours" means all of ours that are not yet on dev; Parts 1–2's files are on dev (applied wherever dev is
   deployed) and are never renamed by this part, so a repeated prefix among dev's own files stops the task for the
